The wider whale activity is not entirely one-sided. One large holder reportedly swapped 16,700 ETH for approximately $30.94 million in USDT, while another whale accumulated 10,380 ETH, worth nearly $19.91 million, despite carrying substantial unrealised losses. These transactions point to different strategies among large holders rather than a uniform move towards selling. Still, the combination of sustained ETF withdrawals and sizeable ETH disposals has added to the market’s cautious sentiment as the token struggles below $2,000.

Ethereum’s derivatives market is showing that traders are becoming more cautious as the price struggles to recover. Open interest across exchanges has dropped to approximately $23.08 billion, down 3.85% over 24 hours. Besides, $241.41 million in ETH positions were liquidated over the past 24 hours, with long positions accounting for approximately 76% of the total.

Funding rates, meanwhile, have moved close to neutral at around 0.0001%. This suggests that the earlier preference for long positions has largely faded, leaving bullish and bearish traders more evenly positioned. Futures activity remains considerably higher than spot trading, with 24-hour futures volume at approximately $47.33 billion compared with $3.10 billion in spot volume. This highlights how heavily ETH trading continues to rely on the derivatives market.

Ethereum’s daily chart continues to show signs of weakness, with the latest decline pushing ETH further below its moving averages. The bearish alignment of the EMA ribbon reflects the loss of upward momentum. A confirmed death cross, where the 50-day EMA moves below the 200-day EMA, would add another warning that the broader trend is turning increasingly bearish.

The order blocks also highlight how sellers have been gaining ground. Instead of facing resistance at one fixed level, Ethereum has encountered successive selling zones at progressively lower prices. Each recovery attempt has struggled to move through these areas, suggesting that sellers are stepping in earlier and making it harder for buyers to regain control. The latest drop below $1,900 adds to this pressure and leaves the market looking vulnerable.

Ethereum is facing pressure from multiple sides, with persistent ETF outflows, reported large-holder sales and a wave of long liquidations weighing on market sentiment. The derivatives market also shows traders scaling back their positions, while the daily chart points to a weakening price structure. The successive lower order blocks suggest that sellers are defending increasingly lower levels, making a sustained recovery more difficult.

For now, $1,829 remains the key support to watch. A breakdown below this level could expose ETH to further losses towards $1,725, while a recovery above $2,000 would be an early sign that buyers are returning. However, ETH needs to overcome the overhead selling zones and improve its broader moving-average structure before the bullish outlook can gain traction. Until then, the risk of another leg lower remains.

Stellar (XLM), the blockchain co-founded by Jed McCaleb, has become the leader in daily market cap growth for tokenized real-world asset (RWA) funds, according to Token Terminal data published by the RWA Foundation. Over the 24 hours to Nov. 13, the market cap of tokenized funds on Stellar went up by $44.9 million, and the network surpassed both Ethereum and Solana.

Over the same period, the market cap of tokenized funds on Solana, Ethereum and zkSync Era increased by $29 million, $10.8 million and $3.5 million, respectively.

Stellar is currently the second-largest blockchain for tokenized funds after Ethereum, according to Token Terminal. Over the past year, the RWA market on Stellar has grown roughly sixfold and reached $4.67 billion, according to rwa.xyz. At press time, the price of XLM stands at $0.1476.

According to the Stellar Development Foundation, Stellar was designed with the requirements of banks and transfer agents in mind. In this context, the compliance tools are built into the base layer of the network, and an issuer can vet investors through trustlines, freeze accounts and claw back assets.

Transactions on Stellar settle in 3 to 5 seconds, and the fees on the network are measured in fractions of a cent. Besides, users can move funds to and from fiat currencies through local providers, which are called anchors on Stellar.

Franklin Templeton's BENJI money market fund has run on Stellar since 2021, and it was the first U.S. mutual fund on a public blockchain.

Today, Spiko, Ondo and WisdomTree are also building their own funds and tokenized U.S. Treasuries on Stellar. Spiko offers euro funds managed by Amundi, and Ondo has launched its USDY token on the network.

In May 2026, DTCC and the Stellar Development Foundation announced that the Depository Trust Company (DTC) will tokenize the assets it holds in custody on Stellar. According to DTCC, DTC-tokenized assets are expected to become available on the network in the first half of 2027.

On Nov. 12, DTCC also announced that it will connect its tokenization service to Solana in the second half of 2027.

#5149. Strategy Sends Crucial Message on Bitcoin's Quantum Security

Strategy, the world's largest corporate Bitcoin (BTC) holder, has sent an important message regarding Bitcoin’s future resistance to quantum computing attacks.

The company, which was co-founded by renowned Bitcoin champion Michael Saylor, recently posted on X that the Bitcoin network can implement new security measures as and when they are needed.

“Quantum-resistant upgrades can be adopted if & when it's needed,” wrote Strategy.

These comments come at a time when the crypto industry is debating whether the rise of quantum computing could, in the long run, threaten Bitcoin’s cryptographic security.

Given that Bitcoin leverages elliptic curve cryptography for transaction security, quantum computing could pose a significant threat to Bitcoin.

A sufficiently powerful quantum computer has the potential to reverse-engineer private keys from exposed public keys. This could give attackers access to the Bitcoin holdings associated with those keys.

At this point, there is no known publicly available quantum computer that can successfully break Bitcoin’s cryptography in this manner.

While speaking at the World Bank in Washington in October, Saylor said that the Bitcoin network would be able to defend itself against any realistic quantum computing threat by coming together and upgrading the software.

Saylor estimated that such an upgrade would take about 90 days once a worldwide consensus is reached on the need for quantum-resistant cryptography.

Saylor also warned against the hasty introduction of new cryptography. He reasoned that more complex security measures may themselves introduce weaknesses.

However, the 90-day estimate has come under scrutiny because such a network-wide shift would involve developers agreeing on technical changes and Bitcoin users moving their funds to new, secure addresses.

Interestingly, Strategy has also initiated efforts aimed at research and development for Bitcoin’s long-term security.

In July, Strategy was part of a group of seven major financial institutions and crypto companies, including BlackRock and Coinbase, that formed the Bitcoin Security Consortium.

The Bitcoin Security Consortium has committed $15 million over three years. One of the areas of focus of the consortium is post-quantum cryptography.

In fact, Bitcoin developers are already working on ways to address the quantum computing issue.

One of the most prominent proposals is Bitcoin Improvement Proposal 360 (BIP-360). This BIP introduces a new type of transaction output, Pay-to-Merkle-Root (P2MR).

Stablecoin Drain, ETF Outflows Leave Bitcoin 'Running on Empty'

The pool of dollars that fuels crypto trading is draining.

Total stablecoin supply fell by $14.2 billion over the 30 days through Nov. 9, the fastest contraction since June 2022, according to a report published Wednesday by onchain analytics firm Glassnode.

The total stablecoin supply now sits just below $280 billion, and the research company suggests that's a big reason why Bitcoin is currently "running on empty."

Stablecoins, tokens typically pegged to the U.S. dollar, serve as crypto’s cash. Traders park money in them on exchanges and onchain before buying other assets.

When the stablecoin supply shrinks, it means holders are redeeming tokens for dollars and pulling that money out of crypto entirely, which Glassnode said leaves “less fuel for a rally.” The firm said a return to supply growth would be the first sign that fresh money is coming in.

The stablecoin drain isn’t the only sign of money leaving. U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs saw about $1.6 billion in net redemptions over 20 trading sessions, the report found, and Bitcoin has traded at a discount on Coinbase, a gauge of U.S. demand.

Bitcoin also slipped below the average cost basis of short-term holders, about $75,600, leaving most recent buyers underwater, and traded near $73,000 on Wednesday. Over $3.6 billion in Bitcoin was recently moved over to exchanges, potentially to be sold, at a loss, according to a separate report from CryptoQuant today.

Glassnode did point to some silver linings. The slide has flushed out most leveraged long positions near the current price, buy orders outweigh sell orders in the order book, and wallets holding between 100 and 10,000 BTC have started accumulating.

The firm flagged $73,000 as key support and said the broader trend change that began in August remains intact as long as Bitcoin holds above its June low.

The contraction comes as stablecoins face growing competition from traditional finance.

Global banks including Goldman Sachs, Citi, and Deutsche Bank are backing a $270 million challenge to crypto’s dominant stablecoin issuers, and the Federal Reserve recently unveiled stablecoin rules on reserves and capital.

#5147. Nakamoto Sells More Bitcoin (BTC)

As per its latest quarterly financials, David Bailey's Bitcoin treasury firm Nakamoto Inc. (NASDAQ: NAKA) has sold an additional 184 BTC from its Bitcoin stash.

Nakamoto Inc., a firm that built its corporate strategy around Bitcoin, held a total of 4,283 BTC as of Sept. 30. The figure is down from 4,467 BTC at the end of June.

Bitcoin Treasuries data shows that Nakamoto Inc. sold 184 BTC in the third quarter of 2026. The firm now has a total of 4,283 BTC in its Bitcoin stash. Nakamoto currently sits in 21st place on the Bitcoin 100 corporate treasury rankings.

The recent company filing indicates that Nakamoto Inc. generated around $13.2 million in proceeds from digital asset sales in the third quarter. However, the filing does not appear to specify whether the 184 BTC were sold in a single transaction.

Nakamoto currently holds approximately $357.9 million worth of Bitcoin despite selling more BTC in the latest period.

This is not the first time in 2026 that David Bailey's firm has reduced its Bitcoin stash.

In March, Nakamoto Inc. sold around 284 BTC worth $20 million to meet working capital needs and fund operations following its acquisitions of BTC Inc. and UTXO Management.

Nakamoto sold its BTC at an average price of around $70,422 per Bitcoin. That was far less than its original Bitcoin purchase price.

In the first quarter, Nakamoto Inc. also received a premium of around 43 BTC from its derivatives strategies before selling around 40 BTC.

Nakamoto Inc. also sold a large chunk of Bitcoin in June.

The company sold around 600 BTC for 35.6 million USDT, as per the company's second-quarter financials.

Combined with proceeds from certain Bitcoin derivative positions, the company generated around $48 million from those transactions.

Nakamoto Inc. used $45 million of that sum to partially repay its Bitcoin-backed loan from cryptocurrency exchange Kraken, reducing its principal amount from 210 million USDT to 165 million USDT.

The recent Bitcoin sell-off comes as Nakamoto continues working to meet its substantial debt obligations while expanding its business operations.

It had roughly 3,030 BTC pledged as collateral for debt as of Sept. 30. That left 1,253 BTC unpledged.

On Nov. 11, Nakamoto Inc. extended the maturity of a 60 million USDT loan from Kraken by one year. The company moved the loan maturity date from December 2026 to December 2027. Nakamoto currently has no remaining principal maturities in 2026.

Bitcoin has fallen below $68,000, extending its decline to more than 20% from its October highs.

US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $1.91 billion in net outflows over seven consecutive trading sessions.

Nearly $1.5 billion in leveraged crypto positions were liquidated in 24 hours, increasing the risk of further downside.

Bitcoin price has plunged toward $65,000, raising fresh concerns about whether BTC could crash toward $60,000. The latest sell-off has pushed Bitcoin below $68,000, while ETF outflows and heavy liquidations continue to weaken market demand. With BTC approaching a critical support zone after several consecutive weekly losses, investors are watching for signs of a reversal. Is Bitcoin heading toward $60K, or can buyers stop the decline?

Bitcoin’s breakdown below $68,000 has shifted the market’s attention toward lower support levels. The cryptocurrency dropped below $66,000 on November 14, reaching its weakest level since August as selling pressure continued through the weekend.

The decline has also extended Bitcoin’s losing streak, putting it on course for a sixth consecutive weekly loss. From its October highs near $86,000, BTC has now surrendered a substantial portion of its gains.

Macroeconomic concerns are adding to the pressure. Hotter US inflation has strengthened expectations of further Federal Reserve rate increases, while a stronger dollar and rising Treasury yields have reduced appetite for riskier assets. That combination leaves Bitcoin vulnerable as investors reassess their exposure to speculative investments.

Institutional demand is becoming another major concern for Bitcoin investors. US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded approximately $185.45 million in net outflows on November 13, extending their withdrawal streak to seven consecutive trading sessions.

The cumulative outflows reached roughly $1.91 billion between November 5 and November 13. BlackRock’s IBIT accounted for a significant portion of the withdrawals, highlighting the scale of institutional selling pressure.

However, the broader ETF picture is not entirely negative. Despite the recent withdrawals, cumulative net inflows across US spot Bitcoin ETFs remained above $54 billion, with total net assets around $86.2 billion.

The immediate concern is whether persistent redemptions will continue to weaken demand. If ETF withdrawals extend into another week, Bitcoin could struggle to attract enough buying interest to establish a durable recovery.

Bitcoin’s decline has also triggered a major wave of forced selling across the derivatives market. Approximately $1.5 billion in leveraged crypto positions were liquidated over 24 hours, with bullish positions accounting for the overwhelming majority.

Bitcoin positions represented a substantial share of those liquidations. When leveraged long positions are forcibly closed, exchanges sell the underlying exposure, potentially accelerating an existing decline.

This creates additional pressure during periods of weak liquidity. Traders who expected Bitcoin to recover are being forced out of positions, while fresh buyers remain cautious about entering before the market stabilizes.

Bitcoin price is approaching a critical technical zone after losing the $70,000 and $68,000 levels. The price action shows a sustained downward trend, with lower highs and lower lows indicating that sellers remain in control.

The $64,000–$68,000 region is now an important demand zone. If buyers defend this area and push BTC back above $68,000–$70,000, the cryptocurrency could attempt a short-term recovery. However, a sustained breakdown below $64,000 would expose the next major support near $60,000–$61,000. That level could become the market’s next significant test if selling pressure continues.

On the upside, Bitcoin needs to reclaim $70,000 before a stronger recovery can take shape. The $75,000–$77,000 region remains a broader resistance zone that buyers would need to overcome to improve the technical outlook.

#5145. Bitcoin Price Crashes to $72,700 as Leveraged Traders Buy the Dip: Is the Bottom In?

The crypto market crash deepens as $1B+ in longs get liquidated. Bitcoin sits mid-range at $72,969; fear at 28 isn’t a bottom yet.

Bitcoin fell below $73,000 on Thursday, November 12, extending a week-long crypto market crash in which traders who bet on a rebound were forced out of their positions again and again.

Bitcoin touched $72,735 on Binance, a hair above Tuesday’s $72,727 low and its weakest price since August 20. It trades at $72,969, down 9.4% from the November 4 close.

BREAKING: $BTC just fell to its lowest level since August.

Over $210 million worth of longs liquidated in the past 24 hours.

The dumping continues… pic.twitter.com/R7NVGivFnD

— Crypto Rover (@cryptorover) November 12, 2026

The altcoins are doing worse. Over seven days, Ethereum has lost 16.4%, Solana 14.7% and XRP 21.3%. CoinGecko values the whole crypto market at $2.42 trillion on Thursday, and Bitcoin makes up 60.5% of it.

Leverage made every drop bigger. More than $1 billion of bets were liquidated on Monday alone, almost all of them longs, the positions that profit only if prices rise. Liquidation means the exchange closes a trade by force once the trader’s collateral runs out, and those forced sales push the price down further.

So is this the flush that ends the crypto market slide, or is there more to come? The data has an answer, and it is not a comforting one.

The sell-off had no single cause. Four pieces of bad news landed one after another:

Each hit forced out more leveraged longs across the crypto market. Thursday’s slide continued the pattern on a smaller scale. We added up every forced closure in Bitcoin, Ether, Solana, XRP and Dogecoin futures on OKX, one of the largest exchanges, over the past 24 hours. Longs lost $27.6 million, against $12.3 million for shorts.

EXPLORE: Bitcoin Price Slides Toward $73K as Nvidia Plunges 9% and MSCI Drops Saylor’s Strategy

Big liquidations usually clear out the crowd. This time, the crowd came back.

In plain terms, traders keep buying every dip with borrowed money. That leaves fuel for another round of forced selling if Bitcoin drops through the next support. Bottoms tend to come when funding turns negative and open interest falls hard, a sign that leveraged buyers have given up.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Next Crypto to Hit 1 Dollar

The Crypto Fear & Greed Index, which scores market mood from 0 (extreme fear) to 100 (extreme greed), reads 28 today. Fear is usually read as a buy signal. The history says it is not enough on its own.

We checked every day since February 2018 when the index sat at 28 or lower, 943 days in all, and where Bitcoin stood later.

This year’s two bottoms came with real panic. When Bitcoin hit $60,000 on February 6, the index read 9. When it bottomed at $57,800 on July 1, it read 11. Today’s 28 is fear, but it is not capitulation, the moment sellers give up all at once.

On the weekly chart, where each candle covers one week, Bitcoin has spent 2026 in a wide range. The low is $57,800 from July 1 and the high is $87,396 from late September. The midpoint is $72,598, almost exactly where Bitcoin trades now.

The price lost its 50-week exponential moving average (EMA), an average that gives recent prices more weight, at $78,219. Its 200-week EMA sits at $69,597. Bitcoin closed below that line for 16 weeks this year, in February and March and again from June to mid-August, and both of the year’s bottoms formed during those stretches.

For the crypto market, three signs would say the bottom is close: the fear index dropping toward the teens, funding turning negative, and open interest falling as longs give up. None has shown up yet. Until they do, the 200-week EMA at $69,597 is the line that separates a pullback inside the 2026 range from a retest of the summer lows.

#5143. Nvidia-Backed CoreWeave Is Surging: Here’s What It Means for the AI Boom

Nvidia-Backed CoreWeave Is Surging: Here’s What It Means for the AI Boom

Nvidia-backed CoreWeave soared 24.7% Wednesday, helping revive the AI trade after weeks of selling, as the company reported surging demand for the expensive computing hardware powering the artificial intelligence boom.

The cloud provider posted $3.66 billion in third-quarter revenue, up 168% from a year ago, and raised its 2026 sales forecast to $13 billion to $13.3 billion. The results also helped lift Nvidia, along with AI infrastructure stocks including Nebius, IREN, Oracle and Applied Digital.

For investors watching Nvidia, CoreWeave offers a useful look at what happens after the chipmaker sells its processors.

CoreWeave buys Nvidia GPUs, installs them in data centers, and rents that computing power to companies developing or running AI models, including OpenAI and other major customers.

That makes its revenue growth evidence that businesses are still willing to pay for AI computing capacity. It does not, by itself, establish that the enormous spending required to supply that capacity will produce sustainable profits.

Nvidia's connection goes well beyond a typical supplier relationship. In January, Nvidia invested another $2 billion in CoreWeave shares at $87.20 each, expanding a business arrangement aimed at building more than five gigawatts of AI data-center capacity by 2030.

The companies also agreed to introduce new Nvidia technology across CoreWeave's infrastructure, including its Rubin platform and Vera CPUs. That makes CoreWeave an important showcase and customer for future Nvidia hardware, not just the chips already installed.

“Together, we’re racing to meet extraordinary demand for NVIDIA AI factories,” Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said when the expanded deal was announced in January.

Nvidia also has a $6.3 billion initial agreement to buy CoreWeave's unused computing capacity through April 2032, subject to the contract's conditions. In practice, the arrangement gives CoreWeave a buyer for capacity it cannot sell elsewhere, while Nvidia gets access to cloud computing built around its own chips.

The relationship explains both the excitement and some of the criticism surrounding AI investment. Nvidia sells the hardware, invests in a company buying that hardware, and has also committed to purchasing some of the computing services it helps create. Inventors call it “circular finance.” AI bros call it a meme. Skeptics call it a warning sign.

Nvidia gives money to OpenAI who gives money to Coreweave who gives money to Nvidia who gives money to OpenAi who gives money to Coreweave who gives money to OpenAi who gives money to Nvidia pic.twitter.com/3UFfK7KwJv

—  Q-Cap  (@qcapital2020) September 22, 2025

Those are real commercial agreements, but the overlapping financial relationships complicate attempts to measure independent demand.

CoreWeave reported $132.5 billion in revenue backlog, meaning contracted business that it expects to deliver over time, not money already in the bank. The company says it is working with customers including OpenAI, Cohere, and Perplexity, and had more than 1.7 gigawatts of active power capacity at the end of September.

“This was a breakout quarter for CoreWeave, with revenue increasing by more than $1 billion sequentially,” CEO Michael Intrator said in the company's earnings release.

The company also expects about $9 billion in customer prepayments and deposits over the next three months. Getting paid before delivering all the contracted services could reduce its immediate need to borrow at a time when investors have become increasingly uncomfortable with the debt financing AI data centers.

The market reaction extended beyond CoreWeave. Wednesday's rebound touched Nvidia shares and the broader technology market, with the Nasdaq gaining 1.6%. CoreWeave's report arrived as investors were trying to decide whether recent AI-stock losses reflected weakening demand or anxiety about the cost of meeting it.

These specialized GPU-rental businesses are known as neoclouds. Some—including CoreWeave, which began as an Ethereum miner—have roots in crypto infrastructure, where operators were already accustomed to running large amounts of power-hungry hardware.

Bernstein analysts described the quarter as “about the best quarter we could have asked for,” according to Reuters, but warned CoreWeave would be among the companies hit hardest if the shortage of available AI computing capacity begins to ease.

The Nvidia partnership does not remove that risk. Newer processors can make older GPUs less competitive, while electricity availability, construction delays, and higher borrowing costs can all squeeze returns. An oversupply of AI computing would also put pressure on the rental prices CoreWeave earns.

On-chain metrics from reputated dashboards like CryptoQuant, CoinGlass, and even TradingView reveal a clear divergence in Bitcoin holder behavior during the November 2026 market correction.

Following a failed late-September rally to $87,153, Bitcoin dropped to the $65,800–$66,083 support zone. While short-term traders and spot ETFs are actively liquidating positions, long-term investors are absorbing the downturn with minimal panic selling.

Current Bitcoin holder behavior shows structural resilience among experienced investors despite immediate spot price weakness.

Tracking Bitcoin holder behavior requires examining total supply held by wallets inactive for over 155 days.

According to CoinGlass data as of November 11, 2026, Long-Term Holder Supply holds steady at 16.24 million BTC.

Rather than distributing into the late-September bounce to $87,153, older cohorts retained their coins, allowing mid-2026 purchases to mature into the long-term bracket.

The Long-Term Holder Spent Output Profit Ratio (LTH-SOPR) currently reads 0.90. Readings below 1.0 confirm that the small fraction of older coins moving on-chain are doing so at a slight loss.

Simultaneously, Supply-Adjusted Coin Days Destroyed (CDD) sits at a subdued 0.94, well below the August 2026 spike above 3.0. Older coins remain largely dormant, proving that conviction holders are not driving the November sell-off.

Recent market entrants display reactive Bitcoin holder behavior during price drawdowns. The Short-Term Holder SOPR (STH-SOPR) dropped from above 1.02 in October to 0.96 in mid-November.

When STH-SOPR fails to hold 1.0 as support, it signals that traders who bought between 1 hour and 155 days ago are exiting at a loss, adding direct downward momentum to spot markets.

The broader market’s Net Unrealized Profit/Loss (NUPL) has compressed to 0.21, placing the network in the lower hope/fear zone.

Historically, NUPL readings near 0.21 indicate that most excess speculative profit has been wiped out. Because aggregate unrealized gains are low, long-term investors have little financial incentive to distribute coins at $65,836.

Exchange flow data confirms that spot selling pressure is stabilizing rather than accelerating. Total Exchange Inflow dropped to 8.1K BTC, while Total Exchange Outflow sits slightly higher at 9.3K BTC.

Net outflows during a price drop indicate that buyers are withdrawing coins to cold storage rather than depositing them onto trading platforms for liquidation.

Analyzing Bitcoin holder behavior alongside institutional flows highlights the primary cause of the November crash.

The 30-day ETF Demand Growth and Apparent Demand metrics have plunged deep into negative territory, reaching roughly -200K BTC in combined apparent demand contraction.

Without institutional ETF inflows to absorb routine selling, even modest retail capitulation pushed price down through moving average supports toward the $65,670–$66,083 horizontal zone.

Note on How to Read This Table: On-chain metrics often reflect two different timeframes at once. The Bearish column shows what is hurting Bitcoin’s price right now (active selling and weak demand), while the Bullish column shows why those exact conditions historically help form a long-term price bottom.

So to keep it simple, the current Bitcoin holder behavior reflects long-term accumulation paired with short-term institutional and retail distribution. Long-term holders are not distributing at $65,800; they hold 16.24 million BTC and keep older coins dormant.

Instead, the drop from $87,153 stems from negative 30-day ETF demand growth and short-term holders selling at a loss. If Bitcoin holds the $65,670–$66,083 support level while exchange outflows continue exceeding inflows, current conditions align with structural bottom formation rather than cycle-top distribution.

The price of XRP fell below $1 on Friday for the first time since mid-August, according to TradingView. The cryptocurrency dropped to $0.9974, and it has now closed in the red for nine days in a row. At the start of November, XRP was trading at $1.30. On Saturday, the price of XRP stands at $1.025.

In the autumn, the price of XRP reached a peak near $1.60, and the cryptocurrency has lost almost 38% since then. Still, the drop has not pushed XRP out of its range on the weekly chart. The lower weekly Bollinger Band is at $0.90, and XRP is still trading above it, so the cryptocurrency is not in free fall, according to the indicator.

The latest decline comes amid a sell-off in U.S. tech stocks after Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO. Traders are also betting on a December Fed rate hike after the October U.S. inflation data, according to CME FedWatch. Bitcoin fell below $70,000 on Friday, and most altcoins went down as well.

Spot XRP ETFs in the U.S. have also seen outflows this week. According to SoSoValue, the funds lost $10.42 million on Nov. 9 and $7.62 million on Nov. 10, and they had no flows on Nov. 11 and Nov. 12. By Nov. 13, spot XRP ETFs recorded net outflows of $18.04 million.

The total net assets of spot XRP ETFs stood at $1.16 billion as of Nov. 12, down from $1.51 billion on Oct. 28. Since launch, the cumulative net inflow of the funds stands at $1.79 billion. The Bitwise XRP ETF remains the largest of the five funds, and its net assets stand at $420.29 million.

According to Santiment, the number of wallets holding at least 10,000 XRP went up by 2,260 over the past 30 days. The number of wallets with 1 million XRP or more stood at 2,147 as of Nov. 13, and Santiment data shows that it is the highest number of such wallets in 2026.

On Aug. 14, the price of XRP fell to $0.986, according to TradingView, and it was the last time XRP traded below $1 before this week.

#5139. Hoskinson Credits Cardano’s Staking Model After Binance Hack Leaves Network Unaffected

Charles Hoskinson has credited the underlying architecture for keeping Cardano (ADA) and Midnight (NIGHT) unaffected by the recent Binance hack, arguing that years of deliberate design decisions are now paying off.

The Cardano founder acknowledged that the network’s early focus on emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, liquid non-custodial staking, and the need for Layer-2 (L2) solutions built around its Extended UTXO (EUTXO) model, came in handy during the hacking incident.

Hoskinson went further, saying these were not accidental advantages but deliberate choices based on anticipating the blockchain industry’s evolving needs. Furthermore, he suggested that the recent hacking demonstrated the importance of building networks with security and resilience at their core.

Cardano’s staking model continues to grow, with the Cardano Foundation reporting that 57.6% of ADA’s circulating supply is staked.

Notably, every delegated coin backs a stake pool that helps produce blocks and secure the network.

Unlike traditional staking models that lock up assets, Cardano’s liquid staking allows holders to delegate their ADA while retaining full control. As a result, they can spend, transfer, or move their funds without first having to unstake them.

Therefore, this approach is unique because it combines network participation with financial flexibility while supporting a decentralized pool ecosystem. Additionally, it reduces reliance on centralized custodians, boosting the network’s broader resilience.

Meanwhile, Cardano is expanding its real-world utility since police in Uttar Pradesh, India’s most populous state, recently began using its blockchain technology to track forensic evidence in active criminal investigations.

More importantly, the Cardano Foundation said evidence scans and laboratory results will be recorded on-chain, creating a tamper-resistant audit trail designed to strengthen the integrity of investigations.

#5138. Jensen Huang Resigns as Nvidia CEO After Second Affair Bombshell: Who Is Colette Kress?

Following Huang’s resignation as Nvidia CEO, who is the Apple exec being tipped for the permanent role, and how has the NVDA price reacted?

Today (November 12, 2026), Nvidia announced that co-founder and longtime CEO Jensen Huang has resigned as President, Chief Executive Officer, and Board member, effective immediately.

The decision follows intense scrutiny over personal and potential national-security-related controversies. The resignation stems from revelations of two extramarital affairs. The first involved Alice Huang, a businesswoman linked to the Singapore-based AI company Megaspeed, a significant Nvidia customer. US authorities have identified her as a suspected asset of China’s Ministry of State Security.

Reports indicated Huang had been photographed with her on multiple occasions, raising concerns about potential intelligence targeting of the Nvidia CEO.

Huang publicly apologized to employees for being unfaithful to his wife but denied compromising national security or company secrets. The situation escalated further when additional reporting alleged a second relationship with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of healthcare and a direct report to Huang.

These dual revelations prompted Nvidia’s board to open an internal investigation and ultimately accept Huang’s resignation after a late-night meeting.

The combination of personal misconduct involving a subordinate and the national-security implications surrounding the alleged Chinese intelligence connection proved decisive.

https://twitter.com/JesseCohenInv/status/2120779503119012207 Colette Kress has served as Nvidia’s Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer since September 2013. Before joining the company, she spent nearly 25 years in senior finance roles at major technology firms,

These firms include Cisco (where she was CFO of the Business Technology and Operations organization) and Microsoft (where she was CFO of the Server and Tools division), as well as earlier positions at Texas Instruments.

She holds a bachelor’s degree in finance from the University of Arizona and an MBA from Southern Methodist University. During her tenure as CFO, Nvidia’s revenue grew dramatically from roughly $4Bn to over $200Bn as the company became the dominant force in AI accelerators.

Volume spiked significantly on the resignation news, consistent with forced liquidations and rapid repositioning. Technically, the contract has broken key short-term support levels, with momentum indicators deeply oversold in the near term.

Any stabilization in traditional NVDA stock would likely be reflected quickly on Hyperliquid, though the platform’s high-leverage environment amplifies both downside volatility and the potential magnitude of a bounce.

#5137. Pressure Mounts on Nvidia's Jensen Huang Amid Reports of Second Affair

Pressure Mounts on Nvidia's Jensen Huang Amid Reports of Second Affair

Nvidia's board is preparing to remove CEO Jensen Huang after reports that he had two extramarital affairs, one with a woman U.S. intelligence believes is a Chinese spy and another with a company executive, The Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday.

The board was planning to meet as soon as Wednesday to determine Huang's future, according to people familiar with the matter cited by the Journal. It was not immediately clear who would succeed him, the paper said.

The New York Times reported on Wednesday that Huang had an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of health care, who reports to him, citing five people who worked at the company. The Journal also reported the relationship, citing a person familiar with the matter.

Nvidia's code of conduct tells employees to avoid situations that create conflicts, including personal relationships, according to the Times. When the newspaper reached him by phone, Huang said, "I don't think you should be talking to me directly," before hanging up. Nvidia declined to comment, and Powell did not respond to requests for comment from either paper.

It is the second affair involving Huang to come to light. The New York Times reported in October that U.S. officials had concluded Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based Nvidia customer Megaspeed, was a Chinese intelligence asset who had developed a close relationship with Jensen Huang. The Financial Times reported last week that a U.S. government memo said the two had been romantically involved. China has denied the allegations.

On Sunday, Huang acknowledged in a letter to staff that he had been unfaithful to his wife, without naming the person involved. He had told Nvidia's board that he had been intimate with Alice Huang, the Times reported, prompting the board to open an independent investigation, led by law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz.

The Justice Department is now leading multiple investigations involving Alice Huang, the Journal reported. Huang also faces a proposed shareholder class action and the threat of a congressional subpoena.

Nvidia shares were down 5.9% at $163.43 in premarket trading early on Thursday, according to Yahoo! Finance data, after closing up 2.9% at $173.73 on Wednesday, before the reports emerged. The stock had already lost about $430 billion in market value on Monday and Tuesday.

Traders expect further losses. On Decrypt Predict, users put an 89% chance on Nvidia trading at or below $160 during regular market hours at some point in November, according to the market. By contrast, they gave just a 6% chance that the stock would climb back to $216 this month.

Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and is its largest shareholder, owning about 3.6% of the company. He has said he does not believe in succession planning, according to the Journal, and the company's latest proxy statement warns that it is "highly dependent" on its longstanding executive team, raising questions over who could replace him.

Potential successors are reportedly under discussion already. One person inside the company told the Financial Times that the simplest option would be to appoint chief financial officer Colette Kress as interim CEO, while two sources pointed to Ian Buck, who runs Nvidia's data center business. Analysts cited Arm CEO Rene Haas, a former Nvidia executive, as a possible outside candidate. "We always knew key man risk was an issue for Nvidia," Bernstein analyst Stacy Rasgon told the paper.

At least one high-profile figure has offered Huang a way forward. Responding to a tweet urging him to hire Huang, Tesla CEO Elon Musk wrote: "That would be an honor."

#5136. Dogecoin ETFs Mark One Month of Zero Activity

As Dogecoin continues to struggle amid prolonged crypto market volatility, its ETF performance has remained muted for the past week, drawing attention from market participants.

Although Dogecoin has retained its position as the king of all meme tokens, institutional demand for the leading meme token has remained on hold as it continues to post deeper price corrections.

Latest data from SosoValue shows that the U.S. Dogecoin spot ETFs have gone an entire month without recording any new inflows or outflows.

More specifically, the two existing spot DOGE ETFs last recorded activity on October 13, when they experienced a combined net outflow of $138,570.

The ETFs became muted the following day, October 14, and neither of the funds has registered a single day of positive or negative flows since then, leaving daily net inflows at zero until November 13.

As such, the Dogecoin ETFs have posted zero flows all month, signaling fading institutional interest in the world’s largest meme token by market capitalization despite its leading position in the memecoin market.

While institutional interest in Dogecoin appears to have declined significantly, both Dogecoin ETF issuers, Grayscale and 21Shares, recorded zero daily net inflows on November 13, confirming that the prolonged period of inactivity remains unchanged.

However, Grayscale's Dogecoin ETF has retained its dominance in the U.S. spot Dogecoin ETF market, holding a total of $9.15 million in net assets, while 21Shares' Dogecoin ETF has held only $1.58 million since its launch.

As such, Grayscale accounts for about 85.3% of the combined $10.73 million in assets held across the Dogecoin ETF market.

US crypto regulation has changed dramatically in 2025, as the Trump administration adopted a more pro-innovation and crypto-friendly approach. Since the start of 2026, the focus has shifted from major congressional reforms to new rules introduced by federal agencies.

This shift followed the CLARITY Act’s failure to pass the Senate. The bill aimed to create a clear regulatory framework for the crypto market, but its failure left regulators to move ahead using their existing powers.

As a result, the SEC and CFTC began introducing new rules, while banking regulators worked on implementing the GENIUS Act ahead of its January 18, 2027, effective date.

In 2026, U.S. regulators have taken a more crypto-friendly approach, focusing on clearer rules and bringing digital assets into the traditional financial system.

In the U.S., short-term capital gains on cryptocurrency held for one year or less (≤ 1 year) are taxed at your ordinary federal income tax rate, ranging from 10% to 37% for the 2026 tax year. Per IRS inflation adjustments (Revenue Procedure 2025-32), the federal long-term capital gains brackets for 2026 are

Beyond capital gains, the IRS also taxes several crypto activities as ordinary income and requires detailed reporting and recordkeeping.

According to a 2026 study by the Pew Research Center, 19% of all U.S. adults have ever invested in, traded, or used crypto, while 40% of men aged 30–49 and 38% of men aged 18–29 report using it.

Among U.S. crypto owners, Bitcoin remains the most popular asset at 74%, followed by Ethereum (53%), Dogecoin (25%), and Solana (20%).

As of November 2026, the U.S. remains the world’s largest Bitcoin mining hub, accounting for about 37.5% of global computing power, or roughly 360–400 EH/s. However, the industry is shifting as miners increasingly convert their power infrastructure into AI and high-performance computing (HPC) data centers.

According to the October 2026 national study by the DeFi Education Fund and Ipsos, most Americans lack confidence in the traditional U.S. financial system and want greater personal control over their money and data.

• 40% of Americans say they are at least somewhat likely to try DeFi if clear access and frameworks are available (consistent with 42% in the prior wave).

• Among those likely to try DeFi, 85% said they would use it to “save money” (up from 77%), 82% said they would use it to “send money to friends or family” (up from 73%), and 82% said they would use it to “earn interest”.

• Nearly 7 in 10 Americans (69%) would use DeFi to receive a payment from work, retirement, or a government agency (up from 58%).

• Only 19% of Americans believe the existing U.S. financial system is secure, while 63% say it needs an upgrade and 74% say changes are needed to give people more control over their own assets

As of November 2026, the US government holds approximately 306,795 Bitcoins, valued at about $20.48 billion (part of a total crypto portfolio worth roughly $20.57 billion).

In 2026, U.S. crypto regulation moved toward greater institutional clarity, despite Congress failing to pass a comprehensive market-structure bill. The SEC and CFTC advanced new rules, while the GENIUS Act established a clearer framework for stablecoins.

New tax reporting requirements also strengthened compliance. However, major issues remain unresolved, including SEC-CFTC jurisdiction, DeFi regulation, and government Bitcoin purchases.

Overall, 2026 marked a shift from regulatory uncertainty toward broader institutional adoption, with the focus now moving to how crypto and traditional finance can operate within a clearer federal framework.

Yes, under current 2026 rules, the SEC oversees crypto assets that qualify as securities (or “investment contracts”), while decentralized commodities like Bitcoin fall primarily under the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC).

The Internal Revenue Service (IRS) classifies cryptocurrency and other digital assets as property, meaning every sale, swap, or spending event triggers a capital gain or loss.

Established by Trump in March 2025, it’s a federal reserve for Bitcoin, initially capitalized by seized BTC, aiming to manage holdings strategically.

In 2026, U.S. cryptocurrency regulation shifted from legislative promises to active agency rulemaking as the SEC and CFTC moved to write market rules after the Senate stalled broader crypto legislation.

In the US, short-term crypto gains (held ≤ 1 year) are taxed at ordinary income rates (10-37%), while long-term gains (> 1 year) are taxed at lower capital gains rates (0-20%), based on your income and filing status. Sources

Shiba Inu (SHIB) is set to get more exposure in the U.S.-regulated financial market after the North American Derivatives Exchange (Nadex) self-certified a new strike event contract tied to the meme cryptocurrency's price.

On November 10, 2026, an official Nadex notice said the exchange certified a swap based on the price of SHIB at a specific time and date. The product, called the Shiba Inu Strike Event Contract, began trading on or after Nov. 13, 2026.

The filing is available through the official records of the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC). The regulator’s database shows that the SHIB Strike Event Contract is certified as a swap, with November 10 listed as the certification date.

The product allows traders to wager that a particular price of SHIB will be attained or surpassed at some point in the future. This opens another avenue for market players to take positions based on the price fluctuations of Shiba Inu without having to buy or hold the underlying token.

Nadex (North American Derivatives Exchange) is a CFTC-regulated U.S. financial exchange acquired by Foris DAX Markets (part of Crypto.com), bringing the Shiba Inu product to a regulated platform.

Shiba Inu Japan community member Kuro reacted to the development, saying SHIB is now the underlying asset for a new financial product in the U.S.-regulated market.

"Nadex, an exchange owned by Crypto.com, has officially filed a new trading product based on SHIB’s price, and it has also been listed in the official records of the U.S. CFTC. This product lets traders predict whether SHIB will exceed a certain price at a specified time, alongside assets such as BTC, ETH, and XRP," Kuro added, saying another opportunity for SHIB to be used in the U.S. financial market has just opened up.

At the time of writing, SHIB was down 3.33% over the last 24 hours to $0.00000414 amid broader crypto market weakness that coincided with strength in the U.S. dollar.

The dollar index reached its highest level since April 2025 on Friday, following hotter-than-expected inflation earlier this week that increased expectations of further Fed tightening, pushing Treasury yields and the dollar higher while pulling down both cryptocurrencies and gold.

#5133. Bitcoin Price Crashes Below $69,000: Is the Worst Still to Come?

Bitcoin news: BTC hit $67,568 as longs were liquidated. Fear is Extreme, but BTC fell further after 15 of 16 past readings.

In Bitcoin news on Friday, November 13, the BTC USD price fell as low as $67,568 on Binance as a wave of forced selling wiped out leveraged bets on a rebound. It was the cryptocurrency’s lowest price since August 19.

Bitcoin trades at $68,772, down 6.7% in 24 hours and 9.1% in a week. Ether lost 5.5% and Solana 3.4% on the day.

BREAKING: Bitcoin falls below $69,000 and ETH nears $1,900 as selling pressure accelerates in crypto.

Crypto markets have now lost -$150 billion in 48 hours. pic.twitter.com/29QW0khxOh

— The Kobeissi Letter (@KobeissiLetter) November 13, 2026

Most of the damage came from liquidations, when an exchange closes a leveraged trade by force once the trader’s collateral runs out. CoinGlass data cited by several outlets put the 24-hour total at about $1.4 billion, close to 90% of it from longs, the bets that prices would rise. Those forced sales pushed Bitcoin through $70,000 in about two hours overnight.

The mood has flipped with it. The Crypto Fear & Greed Index dropped from 28 to 20 on Friday, its first Extreme Fear reading since July.

In Bitcoin news this week, the question is no longer whether the market is scared. It is whether Extreme Fear means the bottom is close, and what the daily and weekly charts say.

The slide started on Thursday afternoon, when Nvidia announced that CEO Jensen Huang had resigned. It picked up speed after midnight UTC, when Bitcoin broke below the $72,727 low from Tuesday and kept falling.

We added up every forced closure in Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP and Dogecoin futures on OKX, one of the largest exchanges, over the past 24 hours.

Investors have also kept pulling money from U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs, funds that buy and hold the coin itself, adding to the selling.

EXPLORE: Bitcoin Price Crashes to $72,700 as Leveraged Traders Buy the Dip: Is the Bottom In?

On Thursday, we listed three signs that would point to a bottom: the fear index dropping toward the teens, the funding rate turning negative and open interest, the value of open futures bets, falling as longs give up. Overnight, two of them showed up.

One sign still points the other way. On OKX, 3.19 accounts are long for every one that is short, about the same as before the crash. Many traders are still buying the dip with leverage.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Best New Crypto to Hodl

Extreme Fear sounds like a buy signal. History says it usually comes early. We found every time since 2018 that the index first dropped to 20 or lower after at least a month without such a reading. There were 16, and we followed Bitcoin for 90 days after each.

The most recent case fits the pattern. Extreme Fear first appeared on June 3 at $64,014, and Bitcoin still fell another 8.5% before it bottomed at $57,800 on July 1. Then it rallied to $87,396 in September.

For anyone reading this Bitcoin news as a buy signal, Extreme Fear says the bottom is getting closer. It has rarely said the bottom is here. A move to the 2026 lows would match the median path.

On the daily chart, where each candle covers one day, Bitcoin sits far below both of its exponential moving averages (EMAs), averages that give recent prices more weight. The 50-day EMA is at $78,226 and the 200-day EMA at $76,325.

On the weekly chart, where each candle covers one week, the key level is the 200-week EMA at $69,555. Bitcoin trades just below it, and the week closes on Sunday.

That line matters. Bitcoin closed below the 200-week EMA for 16 weeks this year, in February and March and again from June to mid-August, and both of 2026’s bottoms formed during those stretches.

The overnight flush did part of the work a bottom needs: leverage came out and funding turned negative.

For traders following Bitcoin news, the Sunday weekly close against $69,555 is the next test. History says the final low often comes weeks after the first Extreme Fear reading.

Bitcoin fell to $62,000 before recovering to about $65,360, a rebound of roughly $3,000. That bounce followed a 16% drop over three trading days, one of the steepest short-term falls of the year.

Measured from the recent high near $87,000, Bitcoin has now lost almost 30%. The token was trading around $81,000 as recently as November 5.

Gareth Soloway, chief market strategist at Verified Investing, sees several forces behind the sell-off:

Soloway also pointed to the upcoming Anthropic IPO as a possible drain on market liquidity. According to Soloway, no major news has come out to suggest that anything fundamental has changed for crypto.

The $66,000 to $67,000 zone had been expected to act as support. Bitcoin spent weeks moving sideways in that range earlier this year, and the heavy trading there built up a cluster of buyers and sellers. Levels like that often slow a decline.

Fear pushed the price through the zone and down to $62,000. Prices rarely reverse at an exact level in a panic, and they often overshoot support before finding a bottom. A drop of about 5% below a major level is within the normal range for a sell-off driven by fear.

If the bounce continues, these are the levels that matter:

The crash has once again punished heavily leveraged traders. Soloway warned that traders using 100x or higher leverage are the most exposed in moves like this. Exchanges and large players tend to push prices into areas where clusters of leveraged positions sit, forcing liquidations.

The overall tone in the market is now one of fear, and extreme fear has often lined up with short-term bounces in the past. The near-term path depends on whether Bitcoin can hold above $62,000 and push back through $66,000 to $67,000.

A recovery toward $70,000 to $75,500 would count as a relief rally inside a larger downtrend. Any longer-term move toward $80,000 to $90,000 or higher remains uncertain and would likely depend on how Nvidia and the broader AI trade hold up.

#5130. Bitcoin ETFs Bleed $1.4B in Five Days as Investors Cut Risk

Bitcoin ETFs Bleed $1.4B in Five Days as Investors Cut Risk

U.S. spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds have recorded five consecutive days of net outflows, as investors retreat from risk assets after a turbulent week for markets.

The funds lost some $1.44 billion between November 5 and November 11, including $299.9 million on Wednesday, according to SoSoValue data. That brings net outflows for November so far to $1.88 billion, after $520 million left the funds in October.

The outflows have coincided with a sell-off in AI and technology stocks. On November 5, when the Nasdaq Composite fell 5.5% in a single day, Bitcoin ETFs saw net outflows of about $430 million.

"This wave of outflows is the result of institutional investors actively or passively reducing their risk exposure following a decline in macro risk appetite, which is not yet sufficient to prove that Bitcoin's long-term allocation thesis has reversed," Tim Sun, senior researcher at HashKey, told Decrypt.

The five-day outflows amount to about 2.6% of the funds' $55.1 billion in cumulative net inflows, "far from a full-scale retreat," Sun said. But the funds' total net assets have fallen to $93.7 billion, down about 45% from a peak of $169.5 billion in October 2025, as both outflows and falling prices take their toll.

Bitcoin is trading at $73,358, down 0.87% over the past 24 hours, according to Decrypt data. On Decrypt Predict, users put a 40% chance on Bitcoin trading above $74,000 on Sunday afternoon, and a 94% chance that it will hold above $70,000. Sun estimated that the average holding cost for spot Bitcoin ETFs is around $81,000, meaning some ETF holders are now sitting on unrealized losses, and that some investors may cut their exposure further as they reassess their allocations at year-end.

Analysts say the bigger concern is a shortage of new buyers. In a note shared with Decrypt, Greg Cipolaro, head of research at BitGo, said the post-election bounce brought only $75 million into spot Bitcoin ETFs, while the supply of dollar-pegged stablecoins contracted 1.9% to $286.3 billion, "suggesting little fresh capital is waiting on the sidelines." Onchain analytics firm Glassnode found that total stablecoin supply fell by $14.2 billion in the 30 days through November 9, the fastest contraction since June 2022, Decrypt reported on Wednesday.

The basis trade, in which hedge funds bought spot ETF shares while shorting futures to capture the price gap, has also become less attractive because the basis has fallen below borrowing costs, prompting many funds to exit, Cipolaro said. That means ETF flows may now reflect directional demand for Bitcoin more directly than before, according to Sun.

Corporate buyers have also slowed. The premium of Strategy's stock over the value of its Bitcoin holdings has narrowed, making it less attractive for the company to raise capital to buy more, while MSCI's decision to exclude it from its indexes could cut off passive investment, Sun said.

"The most critical factor to watch right now is the persistent lack of buying demand itself, the impact of which on prices may be more significant than the outflow figures alone," he said.

Cipolaro said Bitcoin had fallen with risk assets but lagged their recoveries. "Unless it begins to participate in rallies and ETF demand strengthens, digital assets could remain exposed to further downside without benefiting from a broader risk asset rebound," he wrote.

Many people forget just how long the 'winter' was for $GLD. It had an initial burst, even becaming the biggest ETF in world for one day in 2011 ,and then the bad times came and and it (saw 40% of investors bail) and took nearly a DECADE to get back to its that aum high again.… pic.twitter.com/Ny9gyyo1Am

— Eric Balchunas (@EricBalchunas) November 11, 2026

Not everyone sees the outflows as a long-term warning sign. Bloomberg ETF analyst Eric Balchunas compared Bitcoin ETFs with gold ETF GLD, which saw around 40% of its investors leave after its 2011 peak and took nearly a decade to recover its assets, but now holds nearly three times that early high. "Assets without cash flows run purely on sentiment and it changes," he wrote.

#5128. Bitcoin Demand Dries Up as Miners Prepare to Dump 2,077 BTC: Is More Selling Pressure Coming for BTC?

Bitcoin demand weakens as miners transfer 2,077 BTC to exchanges; Antpool accounting for 97% ahead of an estimated 8% mining difficulty cut.

Bitcoin (BTC) demand is showing signs of weakness as miners move more coins to cryptocurrency exchanges. CryptoQuant recorded 2,077 BTC in miner-to-exchange transfers on November 10, approximately 16 times the 30-day daily average of 127 BTC. The move comes as Bitcoin struggles to regain momentum and the network approaches an estimated 8% reduction in mining difficulty.

The latest figures raise concerns about potential selling pressure, particularly as demand indicators weaken across spot and derivatives markets.

Meanwhile, miners could soon receive some relief from lower network difficulty.

Bitcoin's Rebound Fades as Spot Demand Weakens and Miner Flows Surge

“Leverage is being unwound, but spot demand has not recovered sustainably.” – By @xwinfinance pic.twitter.com/n03axjQKqt

— CryptoQuant.com (@cryptoquant_com) November 13, 2026

Explore: Bitcoin Price Crashes Below $69,000: Is the Worst Still to Come?

The 2,077 BTC transfer marked the largest daily miner-to-exchange movement since February 2026, according to CryptoQuant. Around 97% of the transferred Bitcoin came from Antpool, one of the network’s largest mining pools.

The movement represents a significant increase compared with the 30-day average of 127 BTC. Miners often transfer Bitcoin to exchanges when they need to liquidate holdings to cover electricity bills, equipment costs and other operating expenses.

However, CryptoQuant’s Miner to Exchange Flow indicator tracks transfers rather than completed sales. Miners can also move coins for treasury management or other operational reasons.

The latest activity therefore signals a potential increase in available selling supply, rather than confirmation that 2,077 BTC entered the market as sell orders.

Miner transfers are adding to concerns about an already fragile market. CryptoQuant’s 30-day demand-growth indicators showed negative readings across both spot and perpetual futures markets.

Spot demand stood at approximately -280,000 BTC, while perpetual futures demand reached around -82,000 BTC. Combined, the indicators produced a negative reading of approximately 362,000 BTC.

These figures point to deteriorating demand conditions. Spot demand is particularly important because it reflects activity in the underlying Bitcoin market, while perpetual futures activity provides insight into speculative positioning.

The negative readings suggest that buying activity has struggled to absorb available supply. If miners continue transferring Bitcoin to exchanges while spot demand remains weak, the market could face additional downward pressure.

However, these indicators measure changes in estimated demand, not a direct count of Bitcoin sold by investors.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Best New Crypto to Hodl

Bitcoin’s next difficulty adjustment, expected around 14 November at block 975,744, may drop by roughly 8.4% after average block times rose to 655 seconds. The protocol reduces difficulty every 2,016 blocks (about two weeks) to maintain a 10-minute target; slower production eases mining and may boost BTC yield per unit of power.

This could aid miners amid weak prices and tight margins, but profitability still depends on electricity costs, hardware efficiency, fees and BTC value.

Bitcoin is trading near $69,200 after another sharp daily decline. The chart shows that BTC has broken below the $75,000–$76,000 support zone, which now represents an important resistance area. The immediate level to watch is around $69,000.

A sustained break below it could expose the $64,000–$65,000 support area, followed by $60,000. On the upside, Bitcoin would need to reclaim $75,000 to signal a potential recovery and improve its short-term outlook.

Bitcoin faces several challenges heading into the next difficulty adjustment. The increase in miner-to-exchange transfers, combined with negative demand indicators, suggests that the market is struggling to attract sufficient buying interest.

Still, the Antpool transfers should not be interpreted as proof of widespread miner capitulation. The data identifies a large movement from one mining pool, but does not establish that the coins were sold.

The upcoming difficulty reduction could improve mining conditions and help struggling operators manage their costs. However, it is unlikely to resolve the broader weakness in Bitcoin demand.

Investors will be watching whether exchange transfers translate into actual selling and whether spot-market buyers return. A recovery in demand would help absorb additional supply and provide a stronger foundation for Bitcoin’s next move.

Cardano founder Charles Hoskinson has doubled down on his comments about completing the blockchain's development. In an AMA, the Cardano founder was asked about finishing Cardano; he answered in the affirmative, saying yes, the roadmap was done.

In a recent livestream titled "Finishing Cardano," Hoskinson maintains that his job with Cardano was done. "My job is done with Cardano," he said, doubling down on his recent statements and on where things stand with Cardano.

Finishing Cardano https://t.co/LtFVLOHrxk

Hoskinson said he saw a barrage of criticism and negative comments after his remarks, with some speculating that he had failed, that Cardano was a failed project, or that he was leaving Cardano. He, however, maintains that there is no ambiguity in his statements.

Hoskinson revisited the launch of Cardano (ADA) in 2015 in response to critics who claimed that he or the Cardano project had failed.

"So, let's look at 2015. There was a crowd sale conducted to sell ADA into Japan. The price for this was less than 0.2 cents per ADA. And Bitcoin was actually used as the settlement system for this. They bought in yen and settled in Bitcoin. So there are even on-chain records of the sales tranche. The total amount of money raised was $72 million."

Highlighting the growth of the Cardano cryptocurrency, Hoskinson noted that the market valuation has increased immensely from an initial $72 million. "We built a network that went from a $72 million valuation to an all-time high of $100 billion," Hoskinson stated.

Cardano reached an all-time high price of $3.09 on September 2, 2021, which corresponded to an all-time-high market capitalization of nearly $100 billion at that peak.

Following ADA's drop from this ATH, Cardano's market valuation sits at $6.03 billion. Hoskinson maintains that this is still growth, up from an initial $72 million. "Even in its deflated state, everybody's saying it's destroyed and it's a dead coin and all these other things. It's $6 billion. It went from 72 to six," Hoskinson said.

Hoskinson specifically reiterated that the Cardano roadmap is not being abandoned and went on to reveal further growth credentials: "We delivered a fully decentralized, recursively self-improving ecosystem. We left behind a community-led and community-owned treasury that, at its all-time high, had $4 billion in value, and initiated a constitution."

"We built an entire on-chain governance system, wrote a constitution, got the entire community involved, and created a recursively self-improving system that's fully decentralized—the most decentralized cryptocurrency on the planet," Hoskinson added.

#5126. India's Financial Crimes Agency Searches CoinDCX, Delta Exchange Over Offshore Trades

India's Financial Crimes Agency Searches CoinDCX, Delta Exchange Over Offshore Trades

India's Enforcement Directorate has searched three premises in Bengaluru linked to crypto exchanges CoinDCX and Delta Exchange, alleging the platforms carried out unauthorized cross-border transactions worth hundreds of millions of dollars through crypto derivatives and tokenized assets.

The searches were carried out on November 4 and 5 under India's Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA), the agency, India's main financial crimes investigator, said in a statement dated November 6, which it shared on X on Thursday.

ईडी, बेंगलुरु ने क्रिप्टो टोकन डेरिवेटिव एवं वास्तविक विश्व परिसंपत्ति (आरडब्ल्यूए) टोकन से जुड़े बड़े पैमाने पर अनधिकृत सीमा-पार वित्तीय लेन-देन के मामले में फेमा, 1999 के अंतर्गत मेसर्स नेब्लियो टेक्नोलॉजीज प्राइवेट लिमिटेड (“कॉइनडीसीएक्स”) तथा मेसर्स एक्सेलियम टेक्नोलॉजीज… pic.twitter.com/vXwMU5uCTj

The investigation targets Neblio Technologies, which operates CoinDCX, and Excelium Technologies, which runs Delta Exchange. Both platforms offered futures and options on crypto tokens and openly advertised trading in tokenized shares of foreign companies, despite not being authorized to do so, according to the agency.

The Enforcement Directorate alleged that CoinDCX used stablecoins such as USDT to carry out trades for its users on foreign crypto exchanges, including Binance, KuCoin, Bybit and Gate.io, bypassing India's framework for sending money abroad.

When users deposited rupees and placed spot or derivatives orders, CoinDCX converted the funds into USDT and opened matching positions on the foreign exchanges, the agency said. The trades ran through accounts held in the name of a Costa Rica-based group entity, which it described as a shell entity, and were carried out directly from CoinDCX through APIs.

Trades in tokenized shares of companies such as Apple, Google and Tesla were in fact derivatives positions opened on decentralized exchange Hyperliquid, according to the agency.

The Enforcement Directorate alleged that the cross-border transactions in each of these areas ran to hundreds of millions of dollars. It also said CoinDCX holds crypto assets in enterprise accounts on foreign exchanges, and has paid tens of millions of dollars in fees to those platforms in USDT, in breach of FEMA.

The agency said a large share of Delta Exchange's derivatives trading was executed through CoinDCX, and that Delta Exchange had transferred tens of millions of dollars to its overseas group entities, which is under investigation. Their fintech products also appear to contravene India's securities and central banking laws, it said, adding that its investigation is ongoing.

CoinDCX said in a tweet on November 6 that Enforcement Directorate officials had visited its Bengaluru office "as part of a routine enquiry" on November 4, and that it had fully cooperated. The exchange said it operates "in strict compliance with all applicable Indian laws, including FEMA," and adheres to its KYC, anti-money laundering and reporting obligations as an entity registered with India's Financial Intelligence Unit. Trading, deposits and withdrawals on the platform remain fully operational, it added.

Officials from the Enforcement Directorate visited our Bengaluru office as part of a routine enquiry on 4th November. We fully cooperated with the authorities and provided all necessary information and assistance.

As an entity registered with FIU-IND, we regularly…

Delta Exchange said in its own tweet on November 6 that it had cooperated fully with officials, and that its business "does not involve any cross-border transfer of VDAs in any form or manner," using India's term for crypto assets. It said it runs a dedicated rupee-settled exchange for Indian users only, has been registered with India's Financial Intelligence Unit since 2023, and that trading, deposits and withdrawals were functioning normally.

The investigation adds to a difficult stretch for CoinDCX, one of India's largest crypto exchanges. Last month, it confirmed a $16 million loss from retired wallets, days after co-founder and CEO Sumit Gupta called reports of a breach a "false alarm." That followed a roughly $44 million exploit in July 2025.

Coinbase, which has invested in CoinDCX since 2020, won approval from India's competition regulator to increase its minority stake in the exchange's parent company.

#5125. Binance Tightens Security With Zero-Knowledge Proof Upgrade

Binance, the world’s largest crypto exchange by volume, has continued to deploy new measures to strengthen security on its exchange after it suffered the biggest cyberattack ever seen in the history of crypto late last month.

In a bid to foster transparency and regain its users' trust, Binance has just announced the completion of a major upgrade to further strengthen its security.

In an announcement shared on November 14, Binance said that it has generated a new zero-knowledge proof for its Proof of Reserves (PoR) system.

According to Binance, the upgrade allows users to independently verify that it holds sufficient assets to cover their account balances on a 1:1 basis.

The exchange further shared snapshots to prove that it maintains reserves above its users' net account balances across six major cryptocurrencies, boosting their confidence in its operating standards.

It also added that the update covers all assets affected by the recent attack, and the exchange showcased its reserves for the following crypto assets: Bitcoin, Ethereum, Tether, BNB, Solana, and USDC.

While withdrawals are being restored in batches, with the last phase scheduled for next week, Binance has continued to improve its operations to replenish all affected assets and tighten security to regain users' trust.

Following its latest move, Binance revealed that its Bitcoin reserves are currently at 100.05%, slightly above the 100% mark. This means that Binance's Bitcoin reserves amount to about 688,283 BTC, substantially above its net user balances of 687,912 BTC.

The case is similar for the rest of the tokens: Ethereum reserves are at 100.02%, while BNB and USDC recorded ratios of 100.39% and 100.07%, respectively.

While Binance also reported stronger reserve ratios for USDT and SOL, at about 104.34% and 105.86%, respectively, it is evident that Binance holds more of these assets than the total amount owed to users.

Binance has specified that the Proof of Reserves covers assets that are in its custody on behalf of users, rather than its entire corporate holdings, assuring users that their funds are fully backed.

After the largest hack in the history of crypto, Binance has announced that it has fully recovered all $6.3 billion in digital assets stolen during the cyberattack.

For those unaware, Binance initially recovered most of the stolen assets within days using company profits and emergency reserves, while the remaining 10% required additional time.

Well, the hack was so widespread that the operation involved more than 20,000 wallets and at least 65,000 transactions within a week, according to blockchain analytics firm Elliptic.

Of that, around $430,000 was also reportedly laundered through memecoins. Chainalysis also identified Chinese money-laundering networks as part of the cash conversion process.

But now Binance has made a complete comeback, and remarking on this 100% recovery, the exchange took to X and noted,

Once the zero-knowledge proof is generated, users can independently verify that their assets are backed at a minimum of 1:1.

To our users and community: thank you for your patience and understanding.

This coincided with Binance publishing an updated Proof of Reserves snapshot dated 12th November. According to reports, user BTC holdings rose 0.35% to 687,900 BTC, while ETH reserves increased 1.04% to 3.48 million ETH.

Meanwhile, BNB holdings also climbed 1.03% to 42.95 million tokens. However, USDT reserves declined 3.68% to 24.3 billion tokens.

However, the U.S. federal authorities and private-sector partners have frozen more than $2.7 billion in cryptocurrency stolen during the Binance cyberattack.

At the same time, the U.S. Department of Justice also secured court authorization to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion in stolen assets as efforts to trace the remaining funds continue.

This further coincided with the U.S. Department of Justice’s announcement of coordinated actions against North Korean cybercriminal operations responsible for cryptocurrency thefts worth billions of dollars.

In fact, one major operation, called FaceStealer, has reportedly stolen more than $400 million in cryptocurrency over the past 18 months.

Additionally, the FBI also seized cloud infrastructure used in the campaign and more than 900 webcam videos of victims.

#5123. XRP Ledger Activity Hits New November Highs as Batch, Ticket Usage Surge

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Data from XRPL explorer Bithomp reveals that the Batch and Ticket features on the XRP Ledger (XRPL) are increasingly being adopted, with both setting new daily records in November.

The data indicates an increasing use of two XRPL features intended to enhance transaction flexibility and efficiency on the network.

Batch activity reached a new daily high for the month at 1.962 million on November 3, 2026. Ticket activity came next at 1.553 million on November 7, 2026, also setting a new November record. The increase indicates that these features are being embraced in the XRPL ecosystem. Batch functionality allows multiple transactions to be grouped and executed together and was activated on the XRPL mainnet on October 9, 2026.

The growth in batch activity, which neared 2 million on November 3, 2026, comes less than one month after its launch.

This is significant, as Batch is a prerequisite or accelerant for several high-value XRPL use cases already under contract or in the active pipeline, including atomic multi-party settlements. Institutional workflows (custody transfers, DvP settlement, cross-border payment finalization) require two or more accounts to act simultaneously.

On the other hand, tickets provide a way to reserve transaction sequence numbers, giving users more flexibility in managing transactions.

#5122. Morning Minute: Tokenized Stock Venues Are Launching Without Big Tech’s Approval

Morning Minute: Tokenized Stock Venues Are Launching Without Big Tech’s Approval

Morning Minute is a daily newsletter written by Tyler Warner. The analysis and opinions expressed are his own and do not necessarily reflect those of Decrypt. And check out our daily news show 'FOMO HOUR' covering all of the top stories and market action.

🏛️ OKX’s Tokenized Stock Venue Launches Without Big Tech

In September, after the CLARITY Act died in the Senate, the SEC created an innovation exemption letting venues trade tokenized versions of US stocks without waiting for new legislation. It came with one condition. A company that doesn’t want a third party minting tokens of its shares can object in writing within 30 days, and that’s the end of it.

Companies have been objecting ever since. The count at the OKXICE venue went from 22 in October to 50, then 56, and as of its November 5 notice, 67. Every member of the Magnificent Seven is on that list.

OKXICE is launching anyway, on November 23. The venue will list more than 70 assets, though 59 of them are Direxion ETFs. The individual stocks that made it through are Coinbase, Circle, Robinhood, Strategy, BitGo, Securitize and Better.com. Strategy is also tokenizing its preferred shares.

Securitize handles the tokenization, each token is backed one-for-one by a real share and carries dividends and voting rights, and trading runs through Uniswap v4 pools on X Layer, OKX’s Ethereum layer-2.

So a venture between a global exchange and the parent of the New York Stock Exchange built a tokenized equities market, and what it opens with is seven crypto companies and a series of leveraged ETFs.

Notably, this news comes just a day after the NYSE picked Avalanche to handle clearing and settlement for its own 24/7 tokenized securities platform, with a fourth-quarter target for launch after about a year of testing. The NYSE has signed agreements with Broadridge, Computershare, Equiniti and Superstate to support issuer-sponsored tokenized securities and transfer-agent functions. When the company’s own share registry issues the token, there is nothing to veto.

DTCC is doing a version of this too, with a tokenization service that went live October 28 on the Canton Network carrying 20 participants including Bank of America, Citi, JPMorgan and Citadel Securities. Morgan Stanley has already run equities and Treasuries through it.

Progress is being made, slowly but surely. It just gets built slowly, through transfer agents and clearing houses, by the incumbents. Now we wait to see how the market reacts to these first launches…
