#5117. DTCC to Bring Tokenized Stocks and Treasuries to Solana in 2027

DTCC to Bring Tokenized Stocks and Treasuries to Solana in 2027

The Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation (DTCC), the backbone of U.S. securities settlement, plans to bring its tokenized securities to Solana, it announced on Thursday.

The firm will connect the DTCC Tokenization Service (DTS) to the Solana network, allowing eligible assets held by its Depository Trust Company (DTC) subsidiary to be converted into tokens on Solana. The integration is planned for the second half of 2027.

BREAKING: @The_DTCC to tokenize custodied assets on Solana. announced plans to connect the DTCC Tokenization Service to Solana, enabling the tokenization of eligible DTC-custodied assets on the network.

The integration is planned for the second half of 2027, further advancing… pic.twitter.com/gXszWFgUOX

"DTCC is bringing regulated, DTC-tokenized securities to another major blockchain ecosystem, giving market participants greater choice in where they access and utilize tokenized assets," DTCC CEO Frank La Salla said.

DTS went live on October 28 on the Canton Network and DTCC's own private blockchain, built on the Besu framework, with more networks due to be added in 2027, according to DTCC's launch announcement. The service creates tokenized "digital twins" of securities held at DTC, which custodies more than $114 trillion in assets. Solana joins Stellar and Circle's Arc blockchain, which are expected to be added in 2027, according to a DTCC fact sheet.

Under a no-action letter from the SEC, the service is limited to a defined set of highly liquid assets, including Russell 1000 stocks, ETFs tracking major indexes, and U.S. Treasuries. Morgan Stanley said last week it had tokenized U.S. stocks and Treasuries through the service.

Tokens issued on Solana "will retain the same investor protections, ownership rights and regulatory safeguards that apply to traditionally held securities," said Brian Steele, president of DTCC Clearing & Securities Services.

Solana has been actively courting traditional finance in recent months, with Solana Foundation head of institutional Nick Ducoff arguing that, "Institutions choose Solana because it already runs real financial activity at scale." He added that institutions are "already issuing, settling and deploying capital" on the network, in a tweet shared by Solana's official account.

Last month, the Solana Foundation unveiled an open standard for institutional settlement developed with input from J.P. Morgan, and the network completed its Alpenglow upgrade, cutting the time it takes for transactions to become final to roughly 150 milliseconds.

Solana is also lining up more venues for tokenized stocks. Trading platform Formation has notified the SEC of plans to trade tokenized U.S. stocks on Solana, starting with Galaxy and Forward Industries.

On the 12th of November, TRON, Tether, and blockchain intelligence firm Chainalysis jointly launched the Digital Crime Task Force (DCTF), an initiative aimed at identifying and disrupting illicit financial activities involving Tether’s USDT stablecoin on the TRON blockchain.

In this plan, TRON will contribute its blockchain network expertise, and Tether will provide support as the issuer of USDT. Meanwhile, Chainalysis will bring its blockchain intelligence, investigative expertise, and AI-powered monitoring tools.

One of the major reasons behind the initiative is the growing sophistication of crypto-related financial crime. According to Chainalysis, AI-enabled scam operations were 4.5x more profitable than traditional scams in 2025. Meanwhile, impersonation scams increased by more than 1,400% year over year.

DefiLlama further reported that the crypto industry recorded $8.78 billion across 328 hacks in 2026 so far. This is the highest annual loss recorded in its database. In fact, the five biggest hacks together contributed more than 85% of the overall losses.

Interestingly, the number of attacks increased around 2.7 times compared to 2025, while the median loss declined from $1.07 million to $510,000. This suggests that hackers are carrying out more frequent attacks, although most incidents involve relatively smaller amounts.

Seeing this rise, the organizations believe that traditional approaches, which often depend on victims reporting crimes or investigators identifying suspicious funds, are no longer sufficient. Instead, they want to identify potential threats before criminals can move their funds.

Remarking on the same, Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino said,

Criminals are using AI to move faster than ever, and waiting for a victim to report a crime is no longer good enough

This remark comes as Tether has already frozen more than $7 billion linked to illicit activities while working with over 360 law enforcement agencies across 73 countries.

That said, the new task force will therefore be built on these efforts by focusing on proactive investigations and faster coordination. It will also accept tips and asset-freezing requests directly from law enforcement agencies.

Needless to say, the DCTF will investigate several categories of financial crime, including investment and romance scams, stolen funds, cryptocurrency hacks, terrorist financing, North Korean cyber operations, and much more.

This coincided with the FBI recently launching ‘Operation Blackout,’ a coordinated international crackdown targeting scam compounds across Southeast Asia, Africa, and the Middle East that defraud American citizens through fake investment platforms and online impersonation.

Meanwhile, ACAMS has partnered with blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis to strengthen cryptocurrency anti-financial crime training through an updated CCAS certification.

#5114. Sygnum Launches ETH Fund Targeting 8–10% Returns in Ether

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: Sygnum has announced an ETH-denominated fund targeting 8–10% annual returns after fees. The target includes staking income, and investors remain exposed to ETH's market price.

Sygnum is pitching a different measure of investment performance: how much Ether an investor owns at the end of the year. In its November 12 announcement, the bank introduced the ETH Alpha Fund, which opened to investors on November 2 and is aimed at professional and qualified investors in approved markets.

The fund's product page makes two distinctions explicit. Its 8–10% objective is the total portfolio target, including staking. It is also denominated in ETH, so the value of an investment in dollars or another currency continues to move with Ether's price.

That changes how the headline number should be read. As a hypothetical illustration, an investor starting with 100 ETH and achieving an 8% token return would finish with 108 ETH. If the dollar price of Ether fell 20% over the same period, the position's dollar value would still be 13.6% lower.

That example describes arithmetic, not a forecast for the fund. It shows why increasing a token balance and preserving purchasing power are different objectives. The meaning of a successful year depends on which currency the investor uses to measure it.

Sygnum says the portfolio combines native staking with options premiums, arbitrage and derivatives carry or funding strategies. The trading component aims to earn returns without relying on a directional call on ETH.

Ethereum's staking documentation explains the underlying distinction. Validators receive rewards for their role in maintaining the network. They can also lose ETH through inactivity penalties or slashing, while using a service provider adds another counterparty to the arrangement.

Trading income has a separate economic source. An options premium compensates the seller for accepting an obligation; an arbitrage strategy depends on a pricing difference that can be captured after costs. Neither is simply an extra protocol reward.

Combining these activities may diversify the sources of income. It also makes the resulting product more complex to evaluate than a straightforward staking position.

The launch announcement says trading uses Sygnum Protect, keeping collateral off exchanges at the bank. The product page lists a minimum subscription of $100,000 or its ETH equivalent, monthly subscriptions and monthly redemptions, with advance notice requirements. It also lists an investor-level gate of up to 10%, although the page does not explain its mechanics.

Those terms matter for an institution that must meet cash demands on a different timetable. A quoted asset value does not necessarily mean that capital can be withdrawn immediately. A treasury evaluating such a structure has to match its investment horizon with the fund's dealing arrangements.

Custody deserves the same attention. NewsBTC's coverage of Sygnum's MultiSYG lending arrangement illustrates how the control of collateral can be designed separately from the financial exposure attached to it.

This launch sits within the broader expansion of institutional ETH products, alongside developments such as Amundi's Ethereum-based fund share class. The products serve different purposes, even though both use Ethereum-related infrastructure.

For the new fund, the useful evidence will be realised returns, the consistency of those returns and how its strategies behave when market conditions change. Comparisons also need the same accounting basis: net with net, ETH with ETH and equivalent observation periods.

An annual target gives investors an objective to assess. A live track record will show how closely the fund can follow it.

#5113. Why Social Security Cuts Could Cost $500 a Month

Home » Regulations » Why Social Security Cuts Could Cost $500 a Month

A $10.8 trillion payroll tax gap is accelerating Social Security’s 2032 shortfall—and reshaping retirement and investment strategies.

For years, the impending Social Security funding crunch has been framed as a simple demographic math problem: Baby Boomers are retiring faster than younger workers can replace them.

While an aging population plays a role, a new economic analysis reveals a far bigger, largely overlooked culprit—a structural shift in how U.S. income is earned and taxed that has quietly starved the program of $10.8 trillion and shaved a quarter-century off its solvency timeline.

According to a November 2026 study from the AARP Public Policy Institute, the program’s trust funds could have paid 100% of scheduled benefits until 2059 if the share of the U.S. economy subject to payroll taxes had simply held steady at 1983 levels.

Instead, the retirement fund is projected to deplete its reserves in late 2032, putting millions of Americans on track for automatic Social Security cuts exceeding $500 a month.

Social Security relies on payroll taxes for roughly 91% of its annual funding, according to the 2026 Social Security Trustees Report. However, a shrinking slice of U.S. economic output comes from traditional wages covered by that tax.

AARP’s analysis found that wages subject to Social Security payroll taxes accounted for 41% of U.S. gross domestic product (GDP) in 1983. By 2025, that share had fallen to 34%. That 7% represents an estimated $10.8 trillion in lost tax revenue and interest between 1984 and 2034.

The report attributes this erosion to several modern economic shifts:

Under current projections from the Social Security Administration, the Old-Age and Survivors Insurance (OASI) trust fund, which pays retirement and survivor benefits, will run out of reserves in the fourth quarter of 2032.

If Congress were to merge it with the separate Disability Insurance trust fund, combined reserves would last until 2034.

Depletion does not mean Social Security payments will stop entirely, because active workers will continue paying payroll taxes into the system. However, without legislative action, incoming tax revenue will only cover 78% of scheduled retirement benefits in 2032 (or 83% on a combined basis in 2034).

That translates to an automatic 22% across-the-board cut in 2032—reducing the average retiree’s monthly check by more than $500 in over half of U.S. states.

With less than six years before the 2032 deadline, lawmakers face a narrow window to either broaden how the program captures revenue from a shifting economy or let an automatic benefit reduction take effect by default.

A 22% reduction in Social Security payouts would directly compress disposable income for tens of millions of U.S. households, reshaping consumer spending, personal savings rates, and long-term fiscal deficit projections.

First, concerns about the long-term future of Social Security could lead some younger Americans to take more responsibility for their own retirement savings. For some investors, that may mean looking beyond traditional retirement accounts to alternative assets, including Bitcoin and crypto ETFs.

Second, proposals to strengthen Social Security by taxing a broader range of income could have implications for financial markets. If lawmakers eventually target investment income or adjust capital gains taxes, the changes could affect investor behavior and market liquidity across both traditional and digital asset markets.

#5111. SoFi Brings Its Bank-Issued Stablecoin to Polygon’s Payments Stack

SoFi Brings Its Bank-Issued Stablecoin to Polygon’s Payments Stack

SoFi is widening the reach of its digital dollar, bringing SoFiUSD, the first stablecoin issued by a U.S. national bank, onto Polygon’s payments infrastructure as banks and fintechs push stablecoins deeper into everyday money movement.

Polygon Labs said Thursday that SoFiUSD is now live on Polygon Open Money Stack, a payments layer that bundles fiat on- and off-ramps, embedded wallets and cross-chain settlement into a single integration.

The move adds Polygon alongside Ethereum and Solana, the networks SoFiUSD already runs on, and lets SoFi’s more than 17 million members buy, sell, hold, and convert the token on Polygon directly in the SoFi app, without opening a separate crypto wallet or manually bridging assets between chains.

“SoFi is well positioned to bring stablecoins into mainstream finance because it combines the regulatory foundation of a national bank with the reach of a major consumer and enterprise technology platform,” said Marc Boiron, CEO of Polygon Labs.

The expansion lands as stablecoins move beyond crypto trading into the plumbing used to settle card payments, pay businesses, and send money across borders.

On Polygon Open Money Stack, SoFiUSD joins USDC, USDT and PayPal’s PYUSD, and can connect to the wallets, banking rails, and local currencies businesses need for payouts, settlement and cross-border transfers, opening up uses well beyond consumer trading.

The token is redeemable one-to-one for U.S. dollars and issued by SoFi Bank, which is regulated by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency.

SoFi launched SoFiUSD late last year across Ethereum and Solana as the first stablecoin from a U.S. national bank, and it already settles the company’s entire card program over Mastercard’s network. The firm has been building out a broader digital-money suite, recently launching SoFi Earn, a tokenized deposit that pays 4.40% yield and converts one-to-one into SoFiUSD.

For Polygon, the addition deepens a payments business that has become one of the network’s calling cards.

Polygon recently extended Open Money Stack to Solana, and the chain has processed more than $3 trillion in lifetime stablecoin transfer volume, according to the company. Visa and Mastercard support stablecoin settlement on Polygon, while Stripe uses it to route USDC payments for merchants in more than 150 countries.

SoFiUSD is a payment stablecoin, not a bank deposit, and is not FDIC- or SIPC-insured, bank-guaranteed or legal tender.

#5109. Chainstack Traces Customer Data Breach to Exposed Admin Tools

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: Chainstack’s expanded incident report focuses on access-control failures. Its recovery guidance makes completed credential rotation a priority.

Chainstack has added technical detail to the security incident it first disclosed on November 3. Its updated report, with a technical section dated November 10, describes an October intrusion built around configuration and access-control failures. The company says it found no evidence that a software vulnerability was exploited.

According to Chainstack, the attacker entered through a development Grafana instance with unchanged default administrator credentials. An unauthenticated tool server with broad Kubernetes permissions then formed part of the access path. Machine credentials also connected the development and production environments.

The operational lesson is about the reach of an account after the first login. A low-profile testing service can become consequential if it can contact sensitive systems or holds privileges that extend beyond its immediate job.

NewsBTC's coverage of the NEAR AI infrastructure incident explored a related boundary between an application and the services supporting it. The mechanisms differ, but both make the surrounding infrastructure relevant to a crypto platform's security.

The report identifies account names, organisation details, email addresses and password hashes as potentially exposed. It treats node credentials as exposed despite finding no evidence they were read, and asks customers to change passwords, rotate node credentials and regenerate platform API keys where used.

A password hash and a working access token create different problems. Hashes are representations of passwords, while an active token may directly authorise requests. Replacing a login password therefore cannot be assumed to invalidate every other credential associated with an application.

This is why incident guidance needs to identify the affected credential types clearly. A single instruction to change a password can leave developers uncertain about application endpoints, automated jobs and service integrations.

Chainstack's node-management documentation describes a staged rotation process. New credentials are generated while the existing ones remain active. Applications can then move to the replacements before the old credentials are deactivated.

The documentation says both sets continue working until that final step, with no automatic time limit. Completing the rotation permanently rejects requests using the previous credentials. It also says a node rotation does not change a multichain authentication token.

For an operator, the overlap reduces the risk of interrupting a working service while updating applications. The corresponding responsibility is to finish the migration. Generating a replacement alone leaves the previous means of access available.

A useful completion record would therefore track which applications have moved and when the old credentials were disabled. That is a practical control a team can verify after the initial emergency.

Grafana's security guidance warns that services on its local network may be reachable through its data-source proxy. It describes controls such as limiting permitted destinations and using firewall rules to restrict access to sensitive internal services.

Those precautions address what a tool can reach, as well as who can log into it. Authentication and network boundaries perform different jobs; permission limits provide another layer if either boundary fails.

NewsBTC's report on Chainalysis restoring screening services shows why operational recovery and data-exposure analysis can follow different timelines.

Chainstack's expanded account gives customers more detail to assess. The remaining test is whether access changes are completed and whether the revised controls can prevent one compromised service from reaching far beyond its intended role.

#5106. Bitcoin Drops Below $68K as Buyers Quietly Vanish

Home » Bitcoin (BTC) » Bitcoin Drops Below $68K as Buyers Quietly Vanish

On-chain metrics show a massive 362,000 BTC demand gap opening up across major markets.

Bitcoin crashed below the key $70,000 support level on Friday, hitting a three-month low of $67,650 as a sudden leadership crisis at Nvidia, new MSCI index rules, and hot U.S. inflation rattled global markets.

Bitcoin fell 8.6% in 24 hours to $67,650 on early Friday, its lowest mark since August 19, extending a 10.2% weekly decline.

While yesterday’s pullback below $73,000 was driven largely by macroeconomic jitters, Friday’s breakdown reflects a rare convergence of tech-sector turmoil, institutional index risks, and evaporating spot liquidity.

Adding structural pressure to crypto equities, index provider MSCI’s November Index Review has placed Bitcoin treasury companies, including Michael Saylor’s Strategy (MSTR) and Tokyo-listed Metaplanet, at risk of losing their place in major stock market indexes.

Under MSCI’s updated eligibility rules companies that hold too much of their assets in investments rather than running an operating business could lose their eligibility for indexes such as the MSCI USA and MSCI World.

When a company is dropped from a major index, funds that track it often have to sell their shares, which can drive down demand and put pressure on the stock price.

Strategy’s shares dropped 6.49% in extended trading on Thursday. The company has previously warned that eventual removal from MSCI indexes could force passive funds to sell around $2.8 billion worth of its shares.

For Bitcoin, the bigger concern is that Strategy could slow its Bitcoin purchases if it becomes harder or more expensive to raise money. That would remove a major source of buying demand just as U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs have recorded five consecutive days of outflows totaling $1.43 billion, according to SoSoValue.

Market sentiment weakened further on November 12 after Nvidia announced that CEO and co-founder Jensen Huang was stepping down with immediate effect. CFO Colette Kress was named interim CEO.

Huang’s abrupt departure follows an internal board investigation and media reports detailing alleged extramarital affairs, including one with a alleged Chinese spy as well as relationships with Nvidia employees.

Nvidia shares fell as much as 4% on Thursday, extending a month-long decline that has wiped out 27.28% of the stock’s value. The Nvidia news added to pressure on risk assets, alongside declines in the Nasdaq Composite (-0.39%) and S&P 500 (-0.35%).

Rising inflation is adding pressure to both stock and crypto markets. The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics reported that consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, above the 0.3% forecast. Core inflation, which excludes food and energy, also came in higher than expected at 0.3%, against a forecast of 0.2%.

The higher-than-expected figures have reduced hopes of near-term interest rate cuts and raised expectations of a rate hike.

According to CME Group’s FedWatch tool, markets are now pricing in an 88.5% chance of a 0.25-percentage-point rate increase in December. Higher interest rates could put further pressure on Bitcoin by making safer investments, such as U.S. Treasury bonds, more attractive

Blockchain data suggests Bitcoin lacked enough buying demand to defend the $70,000 level.

According to a CryptoQuant report, demand across spot and perpetual futures markets fell by 362,000 BTC over 30 days, with spot demand declining by 280,000 BTC and futures demand by 82,000 BTC.

Meanwhile, Bitcoin miner transfers to exchanges surged to 2,077 BTC on November 10, roughly 16 times the 30-day daily average of 127 BTC. About 97% of the transfers came from Antpool.

At the same time, stablecoin supply contracted by $14.2 billion over 30 days, pointing to declining liquidity across the crypto market.

According to CryptoQuant analysts, the broader picture remains cautious. Leverage is being unwound, but fresh spot buying has yet to return convincingly. Until demand strengthens, ETF flows turn positive and market liquidity stabilizes, Bitcoin’s recovery is likely to remain fragile, with further downside risks still in play.

#5105. Solo Brings Human Verification to Venmo Co-Founder’s JellyJelly App as AI Agents Beat CAPTCHA

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

Solo’s SDK confirms that each JellyJelly account belongs to a real, unique person, after a Solo AI agent passed CAPTCHA on 50+ Discord servers.

Magdon-Ismail is co-founder and CEO of JellyJelly and an advisor to Solo. He co-developed the SDK behind the integration, shaping both its architecture and the way new users are onboarded.

The move comes as AI agents learn to pass the tests meant to keep them out. In an experiment run by Solo, an AI agent named Gary joined more than 50 Discord servers overnight and sent over 500 messages. No one identified it as an AI agent.

Gary had two instructions: pass every CAPTCHA challenge and accept the terms of service. It completed both through ordinary browsing and clicking, without any custom exploits.

Solo reads the result as a weakness in CAPTCHA. The challenges test whether a visitor can solve a puzzle, and capable AI agents can solve the same puzzles. Harder tests add friction for legitimate users, but they do little to show that a human is behind an account.

“CAPTCHA was built around the idea that humans could do things bots couldn’t. That’s becoming a harder assumption to make when AI agents can browse, click and solve the same challenges as people,” said Edison Siu, co-founder and CEO of Solo. “Our approach is to verify the human directly. Platforms need to know they’re dealing with a real person. Users shouldn’t have to struggle through more puzzles or upload identity documents to prove it.”

JellyJelly lets users share short videos and send cryptocurrency payments to one another. The rise of AI-generated video and automated accounts has made it harder for social platforms to know who is behind each account. Solo’s SDK brings human verification into that setting. It helps the platform tell genuine users from automated accounts, and it stops one person from registering several verified identities.

The process starts with a facial scan from a standard smartphone camera. Solo converts the scan into a biometric representation and encrypts it on the device using fully homomorphic encryption (FHE). This type of encryption lets a system work on data without ever decrypting it. Solo uses it to compare the encrypted representation against existing records, so the matching step never exposes the underlying data.

Users do not need special hardware or a government-issued ID. Raw facial images are not stored. Apps that use the SDK receive a verification result, not access to anyone’s biometric information.

The same SDK can be added to gaming platforms, payment services and other applications that need to block duplicate accounts or separate real users from automated activity.

Solo is backed by Draper Associates, the venture firm founded by Tim Draper. Draper Associates led a $1 million round in the company in March 2025. Solo was also selected for cohort 5 of the Solana Incubator.

Solo’s human verification technology is already live. The company is now working on tools that would let verified users authorize their own AI agents, so merchants and online platforms can confirm that a real, unique person stands behind each one. Solo also plans to enable AI agents and AI companies to pay verified people for work that only humans can do.

Magdon-Ismail, who co-founded Venmo and helped develop its peer-to-peer payment system, is advising Solo on how people and their AI agents will pay and get paid.

“Venmo made it easy to pay a friend,” said Magdon-Ismail. “The next step is your AI agent paying on your behalf. The business receiving that payment needs to know a real person authorized it. I’m working with Solo to make that process simple for everyone involved.”

Solo develops proof-of-humanity technology that lets online platforms check that a user is a real, unique person, without asking who that person is. Its smartphone-based system uses fully homomorphic encryption to compare encrypted biometric data, and partners receive a verification result instead of raw biometric data. Solo provides an SDK for web and mobile applications. The company is backed by Draper Associates and was selected for the Solana Incubator cohort 5. Its first product, SoloMission, lets AI agents collect feedback from verified humans.

Thailand’s Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has proposed a set of new rules to regulate stablecoin transactions conducted through licensed digital asset operators.

Announced on 12th November, the draft notification aims to prevent cryptocurrencies and stablecoins from being used for money laundering, cybercrime, and bypassing regulations governing international money transfers.

Here, it’s worth noting that this update came soon after September’s public consultation. During the same, the regulator collected feedback from industry participants.

As it stands, the SEC has incorporated those changes into the latest draft. It is now seeking further public comments until 26th November.

In this, one of the key proposals is to introduce a daily transfer limit of 5 million Thai baht per customer at each regulated digital asset operator. That said, the limit would apply separately to incoming and outgoing stablecoin transfers. However, the value of these transactions must also be consistent with the customer’s declared income and financial position.

However, it’s important to note that transfers between a customer’s own accounts at two SEC-supervised operators would be exempt from the limit, provided both operators follow the Travel Rule.

Simultaneously, the SEC also wants to strengthen wallet ownership verification. In this, the SEC has enabled customers to deposit stablecoins from their own verified wallets and withdraw them to wallets registered in their names.

Additionally, operators would also need to follow the Travel Rule, analyze customers, identify suspicious accounts, and track transactions connected to high-risk wallets.

These requirements would be done in order to make it harder for criminals to move illicit funds through regulated platforms.

Finally, the proposal also introduces stricter responsibilities for exchanges and brokers. Exchanges would have to publicly disclose their market makers and the digital assets for which they provide liquidity. Meanwhile, brokers would be prohibited from using liquidity providers for stablecoin-to-Thai baht trading pairs.

Besides that, brokers and dealers offering off-platform transactions would face a minimum transaction threshold of 3 million baht and would have to publish trading prices for transparency. Brokers would no longer be allowed to arrange off-platform trades directly between customers.

Taken together, these steps would help the SEC combat crimes that are concerning the stablecoin ecosystem in Thailand.

#5103. Jensen Huang Resigns as Nvidia CEO, With CFO Colette Kress Named Interim Chief

Jensen Huang Resigns as Nvidia CEO, With CFO Colette Kress Named Interim Chief

Jensen Huang has resigned as CEO of Nvidia, ending a 33-year tenure at the helm of the chipmaker he co-founded, after reports of affairs with a suspected Chinese spy and a senior company executive.

Huang has stepped down as president, CEO and a member of the board, effective immediately, Nvidia said on Thursday. Colette Kress, Nvidia's chief financial officer since 2013, will serve as interim CEO while remaining CFO, as the board searches for a permanent successor from both inside and outside the company. Nvidia did not give a reason for Huang's resignation, but thanked him for his "immeasurable contributions to the company and the industry."

NVIDIA announces CEO transition. Read the release: https://t.co/MTTUvFHCJA

— NVIDIA Newsroom (@nvidianewsroom) November 12, 2026

The board also named Harvey Jones, a former CEO and executive chairman of chip design software company Synopsys, as its first-ever chair.

"The Board has full confidence in Colette and the leadership team, and we expect the company's operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption," Jones said.

Kress said she was "committed to building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years." Nvidia will report its third-quarter results as scheduled on Tuesday, the company said.

Nvidia shares were down 7.7% at $160.28 shortly after the market opened on Thursday, having fallen as low as $148.80, according to Yahoo! Finance data.

Huang's departure comes four days after he acknowledged in a letter to staff that he had been unfaithful to his wife, prompting Nvidia's board to open an independent investigation. He had told the board that he had been intimate with Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based Nvidia customer Megaspeed, The New York Times reported.

The Times had reported in October that U.S. officials had concluded Alice Huang was a Chinese intelligence asset, while the Financial Times later reported that a U.S. government memo said the two had been romantically involved. China has denied the allegations.

On Wednesday, the Times reported that Huang had also had a relationship with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of health care, who reports to him. The Wall Street Journal later reported that the board was preparing to oust him, adding to the pressure on the CEO.

The scandal has wiped hundreds of billions of dollars off Nvidia's market value, with the company losing about $430 billion in two days earlier this week. Nvidia and Huang also face a proposed shareholder class action, and lawmakers had threatened to subpoena him.

Huang ran Nvidia with about 60 executives reporting directly to him and has said he did not believe in succession planning, leaving the company without an obvious successor.

Prior to the announcement of Huang's resignation, one person inside the company had told the Financial Times that naming Kress as interim CEO would be the simplest option. Other potential candidates cited by the paper's sources include Ian Buck, who runs Nvidia's data center business, and Arm CEO Rene Haas, a former Nvidia executive.

Huang remains Nvidia's largest shareholder, with a stake of about 3.6%, according to the Journal.

#5101. NYSE Taps Avalanche to Power Tokenized Stock Trading as Wall Street Embraces Blockchain Infrastructure

Home » Exchanges » NYSE Taps Avalanche to Power Tokenized Stock Trading as Wall Street Embraces Blockchain Infrastructure

NYSE has selected Avalanche technology to support settlement for its planned tokenized securities platform, bringing round-the-clock stock trading and faster settlement closer to reality, pending regulatory approval.

The New York Stock Exchange is mixing together blockchain technology and traditional finance. It selected Avalanche to power the settlement infrastructure of its upcoming tokenized securities platform. The decision is part of a growing effort to bring crypto trading and its benefits to traditional finance.

Announced on November 9, 2026, the partnership will see Avalanche provide the core ledger technology for the clearing firm supporting the NYSE-affiliated digital trading venue. One of the goals is to enable round-the-clock trading, as well as clearing and settlement of tokenized securities, all of which still require regulatory changes.

NYSE has organized a yearlong test, and afterwards Avalanche emerged as a favorite provider and one that could meet its needs and provide a seamless inclusion of blockchain traders into the fold of the stock exchange account holders.

The platform is designed to support equities issued across multiple blockchain networks, meaning Avalanche will not necessarily host every tokenized stock traded through the venue. The technology will therefore mostly be used to record and settle transactions.

NYSE Head of Digital Issuance Dennis Lee said that the focus was on speed, reliability, and predictable costs. Ava Labs CEO Emin Gün Sirer also highlighted the importance of dedicated infrastructure.

The crypto infrastructure industry is huge, and there’s a growing list of cryptocurrency exchanges, including those reviewed by CryptoManiaks, to choose from. Platforms made for transfers and smart contracts automating payments have also grown and now include thousands of providers. NYSE chose Avalanche due to some of its unique characteristics.

Avalanche’s architecture allows businesses to create dedicated blockchain networks with rules tailored to their operational and regulatory requirements. It creates a flexibility that traditional financial institutions are looking for.

Stock exchanges handle countless transactions, and stability is the most important feature they are looking for. Another important feature is atomic settlement. It allows the transfer of securities and corresponding payment to occur as part of the same transaction. Therefore, there’s no chance one side of a trade is completed while the other remains outstanding.

NYSE also plans to operate a custom blockchain built using Avalanche technology rather than relying directly on Avalanche’s public network.

The decision reflects a broader effort to tokenize traditional markets and get the best of both worlds. That way, crypto companies won’t dominate the space, but can combine their features with those of the stock market.

Nasdaq is among the NYSE’s most prominent competitors. It, too, has developed tokenized stock infrastructure and is pursuing partnerships that could help distribute blockchain-based securities. This is done in cooperation with Kraken and in a way that NYSE is responding to the demands of a competitive market.

The Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation (DTCC), a central institution in US securities settlements, also has plans to introduce tokenization. It plans to use blockchain to support securities custody and transfers.

NYSE has also expanded its list of partners. It now includes Broadridge Financial Solutions, Computershare, Equiniti, and Superstate. These developments show that financial institutions are fighting to establish the underlying infrastructure that will determine how digital securities are traded, transferred, and settled.

What Tokenized Stocks Could Mean for Investors

Tokenized stocks could change how investors are accessing traditional financial markets. The possibility of trading outside of business hours is the first thing investors have been looking for, alongside faster settlements. The NYSE’s broader platform plans include stablecoin-based funding, fractional share trading, and immediate settlement.

Ownership will also change. The NYSE has indicated that its platform will support tokenized shares that are fungible with traditionally issued securities, as well as securities originally issued in digital form. Shareholders will continue to have the same rights as traditional owners, meaning they’ll receive dividends and take part in corporate governance.

All of these benefits aren’t regulated, and before investors can take advantage of them, traditional regulatory bodies need to act and establish rules and guidelines for the new features.

Despite the institutional interest, the NYSE’s Avalanche-powered project still faces several challenges before it can become a functioning alternative to conventional securities infrastructure. The platform needs to demonstrate that it can maintain the safeguards expected of a major US stock exchange.

There’s also a distinction between Avalanche’s institutional adoption and the potential benefits for its native AVAX token. It’s not clear if the cooperation with NYSE will generate demand for AVAX. The project will depend on its ability to attract issuers, brokers, and investors while delivering reliable settlement.

The AI Compute Race report prices GPU compute outside the biggest buyers: a three-year commitment cuts the median price by 48%, while 17 of 22 tracked GPU models rose in price over the past year

DALLAS, Texas – November 13, 2026 – Fluence has published The AI Compute Race, a report that prices GPU cloud compute for every company that is not a frontier lab or a hyperscaler. It was produced with research partners NEAR AI, io.net, Boundless, Phala, Gensyn, Fortytwo, Theta, Compute Labs and GAIB. Its central finding: where a company buys a GPU-hour sets the price. Across H100, H200 and B200 models, hyperscalers list GPUs at 1.98 times the GPU-cloud median, from 1.4 times on the B200 to 2.8 times on the H100. The same H200 lists from $4.08 to $10.60 an hour.

Commitment length matters almost as much as provider choice. Against each provider’s own on-demand rate, a one-year reservation cuts the median price by 21% and a three-year term by 48%. Spot capacity lists at 53% of on-demand, for workloads that can be interrupted.

Buyers who expect GPU prices to fall may need to recheck their budgets. Seventeen of the 22 GPU models tracked by GetDeploying cost more than a year earlier, and the median H100 rents for 13% to 30% more, depending on the window measured.

The report also traces why prices are rapidly rising:

“Open-weight models are close behind the best closed ones, and companies are switching to them. Any company with GPUs can now serve a near-frontier model on hardware it controls. The GPUs are the hard part,” said Evgeny Ponomarev, Co-founder of Fluence.

The report closes with four ways to pay less for the same compute: compare the same chip across provider types, commit when the workload is steady, match the GPU generation to the model, and look beyond the hyperscalers, since much of the newest neocloud capacity is contracted to labs years ahead.

The full report is available at fluence.ai/compute-race-2026.

Fluence Cloud is a GPU cloud provider with capacity from independent data centers (fluence.ai). #5097. Tether Gold Gets Clean KPMG Audit Confirming $2.2B in Physical Gold Backing

Tether Gold Gets Clean KPMG Audit Confirming $2.2B in Physical Gold Backing

Tether's gold-backed stablecoin, Tether Gold (XAUT), has completed its first full audit by KPMG, which found the token fully backed by physical gold, the company announced on Thursday.

KPMG issued an unqualified opinion on the financial statements of TG Commodities, which issues XAUT, for the year ended December 31, 2025. An unqualified, or "clean," opinion means the auditor found that the statements fairly present the company's financial position, without reservations.

Tether Gold (XAU₮) Becomes Tether’s Second Stablecoin to Complete a Big Four AuditLearn more: https://t.co/eO0asUwvlI

As of the end of 2025, TG Commodities held 520,089.350 troy ounces of allocated gold, valued at $2.246 billion, against 520,089.300 XAUT tokens in issue, according to Tether. The gold is held in vaults in Switzerland, and each token represents an ownership interest in gold on specific bars.

As part of the audit, KPMG physically counted and inspected every gold bar backing the token, rather than relying only on confirmations from custodians, Tether said.

"KPMG counted every single bar as part of its Tether Gold audit," Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino said, adding that he believes XAUT "is on track to become the first true competitor to the gold ETF market."

The XAUT audit is Tether's second by a Big Four firm. In August, KPMG issued a clean opinion on Tether International, the issuer of its flagship USDT stablecoin, in what the company called the largest inaugural audit in history, Decrypt reported at the time.

For years, Tether faced criticism for relying on quarterly attestations, which offer a snapshot of reserves at a single point in time, rather than a full audit of its finances. The company first said earlier this year that it was being audited by a Big Four firm without naming it, before confirming KPMG.

Tether still publishes quarterly attestations for USDT. Its latest, prepared by accounting firm BDO and covering the period to September 30, showed total reserve assets of $191.5 billion against $183.5 billion in liabilities, giving it an excess reserve buffer of almost $8 billion, according to the report. Tether said it made $1.5 billion in net operating profit in the third quarter.

"These milestones advance the progress towards audits across the whole of Tether," said chief financial officer Simon McWilliams.

Separately from the gold backing XAUT, Tether has also built up its own large gold reserves, and Ardoino has said it will keep adding to its stash, which it stores in a former nuclear bunker in Switzerland.

#5096. Bitcoin Slides Toward $63,000 as Weekend Selling Tests Market Confidence

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

Bitcoin's latest decline is testing something more important than a round-number price level: whether buyers have enough conviction to absorb selling when liquidity thins out over the weekend. The market slipped toward $63,000 during Saturday's trading after a difficult week for digital assets, leaving traders debating whether the move represents a final flush or simply another stage of a broader retreat.

The distinction matters. A sharp fall can produce attractive entry points, but it can also expose how quickly leveraged positions and thin order books amplify one another. The latest numbers are a snapshot of trading on November 14, not a live quote or a forecast for the week ahead.

CoinDesk reported that Bitcoin traded down to roughly $63,400 on Saturday, with its weekly decline exceeding 15% at that point. Ether and several major altcoins had experienced even larger weekly percentage losses. That broader weakness is worth highlighting because it suggests the pressure was not confined to a single Bitcoin-specific headline or one isolated exchange.

Weekend trading can be particularly unforgiving. Liquidity providers may quote less aggressively, while automated liquidation systems do not take Saturdays off. A relatively modest amount of spot selling can therefore travel further through the order book than it might during busier weekday sessions. It is a possible amplifier, though not proof that liquidations caused the entire move.

The decline also arrives against a more cautious institutional backdrop. US spot Bitcoin funds have recorded a prolonged run of net withdrawals, extending the selling discussed in NewsBTC's earlier report on Bitcoin ETF outflows. These products do not dictate Bitcoin's price, but their flows provide one measurable indication of whether an important group of investors is adding exposure or reducing it.

There is an important mechanical distinction here. A fund's net outflow is not necessarily a direct measure of total Bitcoin sold in the wider market, and changes in assets under management also reflect price movements. Still, a sustained absence of fresh fund demand can leave the spot market with less of a cushion when other holders decide to sell.

On-chain analyst James Check has described the environment in terms of capitulation, according to CoinDesk. That captures the emotional side of the market: investors who tolerated earlier drawdowns finally decide they would rather hold cash than wait for a rebound. But a capitulation narrative is not a timestamped bottom signal. Markets can experience several waves of forced or reluctant selling before stabilising.

A more useful test is what happens after the initial bounce. Does Bitcoin hold its recovery on increasing spot participation, or does the rebound fade as soon as volatility eases? Are funding rates, exchange balances and ETF flows telling a consistent story, or are they pulling in different directions? Answers to those questions carry more weight than a declaration that the market looks cheap.

Traders are also processing a changing interest-rate outlook and the implications of recent US inflation figures. NewsBTC's analysis of October CPI and the rate backdrop offers useful context: Bitcoin can behave like a high-beta risk asset when expectations for borrowing costs change abruptly, even when the longer-term investment thesis is framed around monetary independence.

For the coming week, watch whether trading volumes improve as US markets reopen and whether Bitcoin can defend its weekend range without relying on a short-lived derivatives squeeze. The latest slide deserves attention, but it does not, on its own, settle the argument about where the cycle goes next.

According to Fire Hustle, monthly volume climbed from roughly $100 billion in January to $800 billion in August, with stocks accounting for 62.3% of activity.

The expert identifies Hyperliquid as the closest to strengthening that connection. Trade.XYZ, which operates most of the platform’s traditional-market contracts, reportedly splits trading fees equally with Hyperliquid, whose share largely supports HYPE buybacks.

There is a catch: Trade.XYZ is operating with trading fees discounted by more than 90% to attract users. The YouTube video says those discounts are expected to shrink as markets mature, potentially increasing buyback funding, although higher fees could also change trading behavior.

ONDO presents a different problem. Fire Hustle says Ondo Finance surpassed $4 billion in total value locked, including more than $1.3 billion in tokenized stocks and ETFs, while ONDO holders currently receive no direct fee distributions, buybacks or burns.

A holder-led forum proposal would direct 20% of revenue toward token buybacks and burns, eventually rising to 40%. The host stresses that it is not an approved policy and says the team had not responded.

Crucially, the $4 billion figure represents assets deposited, not revenue available to distribute.

Injective already links application revenue to INJ buybacks and burns, according to the video. But its scale remains modest: the host cites roughly $215 million in traditional-market trading over 30 days and a largest buyback round of about $315,000.

The potential catalyst is Pineapple Prime, a planned mortgage-yield product.

More than $1 billion in mortgage records reportedly moved onto Injective, but the host makes an important distinction: those records are data, not yet money flowing through a live investment product.

In conclusion, these are three way different bets: higher fee capture, an unapproved governance change and a product launch.

None makes trading growth equivalent to token returns, especially when discounted fees, limited activity and concentrated infrastructure can interrupt the connection.

#5094. Analyzing why Celestia’s 21M TPS claim comes with THREE big catches after TIA’s 8% drop

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Celestia [TIA] has had a packed month so far. Their latest breakdown of how Voyager works also has people talking.

This discussion misses the most important question though — Is TIA’s price keeping up?

In the month gone by, Celestia launched Eden, an EVM chain for testing how AI agents trade.

Fibre went live on mainnet on 20th October, adding a lane for data uploads of around 128MB, up from 8MB. On the 29th, they launched Voyager, a payments layer for AI agents.

TIA perps also got listed on Decibel on 4th November. Of all these, Voyager’s been the people’s pick so far.

In a recent blog, Blazej Kolad, Staff Protocol Engineer at Celestia, explained how it hit over 21 million TPS across 100 million accounts.

What’s surprising is that it doesn’t split the work across lots of cores. Main execution runs on a single thread.

They’re arguing that memory is the real bottleneck, and one core with the right data close by can do much and more.

There are catches, though. Voyager isn’t on mainnet yet. The benchmark skipped signature checks, and crash recovery still isn’t ready.

At the time of writing, TIA was trading at $0.40. For context, that’s an 8.7% dip over just 24 hours.

We’re a long way from mid-October. Around the time Eden launched, TIA climbed so high, it traded close to $0.76. Since then, however, it’s been dipping steadily. Now, it’s at half of that peak.

The big unlock of 31st October (which added about 5.58 million TIA to the market) didn’t help either. For most of November, TIA had been trading between $0.41 and $0.45 so far. Today though, it pierced through the bottom of that range.

The RSI was at 38.2, having briefly crossed above it on the 12th. However, that didn’t last.

Simply put, the tech’s getting all the praise. However, the token’s not reflecting any of it. Not yet.

#5093. New Monero Privacy Update Might Be Coming Soon: Key Improvement

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. We believe that all content is accurate as of the date of publication, but certain offers mentioned may no longer be available.

Monero contributor has opened a pull request that changes how nodes relay transactions coming from Tor and I2P, according to the project's GitHub.

PR 11743 was opened on November 13 and is currently pending review. It is an updated version of a PR opened on November 8 by contributor vtnerd. After receiving feedback from another Monero developer, vtnerd, the PR was updated.

The issue lies in a mechanism where a node receives a transaction over Tor or I2P and then passes it to the regular Monero network.

Currently, when a Monero node receives a transaction over Tor or I2P, it relays that transaction to the rest of the Monero network.

While the transaction is technically private as it travels into the node, once it reaches Monero's public peers, the transaction is no longer private. This PR proposes that Monero nodes will only accept transactions from Tor and I2P peers over incoming connections. Transactions received over outgoing Tor and I2P connections would be ignored.

Once accepted, the transaction would be subject to a random delay before being relayed to the rest of the Monero network using Monero's existing transaction relay protocol, Dandelion++. Currently, a user can instruct their node to broadcast their transaction immediately.

Over Tor and I2P connections, this request would be ignored. No transaction would be exempt from the random delay.Being able to link a transaction's timing between the anonymity network and the Monero network is an easy way to deanonymize a user. If a transaction is broadcast to the Monero network immediately after being received from Tor, an observer watching both networks can link the two.

This is a similar concept to a previous PR from vtnerd that would have introduced a randomized delay when relaying transactions from Tor and I2P to the Monero network.

While the amount of code that would need to be modified is not particularly large, this does close a hole for users that rely on Tor and I2P to obscure their location.

When the patch lands in a release is yet to be confirmed. The PR is also labeled for a backport, so it might reach the current release branch as well.

#5092. Bitcoin ETFs Lose $2.35 Billion in Two Weeks as Outflow Streak Extends

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds have now suffered two consecutive weeks of withdrawals exceeding $1 billion, a remarkable reversal for products often treated as the clearest gauge of institutional demand. The latest weekly tally also extends the run of daily redemptions to seven trading sessions. That does not mean every institutional holder is selling Bitcoin, but it does remove one of the market's more visible sources of buying support.

The numbers cover the trading week ending Friday, November 13, and are based on reported fund-flow data. They should not be confused with changes in fund valuations caused by Bitcoin's falling price.

According to The Block's analysis of SoSoValue data, US spot Bitcoin ETFs registered approximately $1.07 billion of net outflows for the week. The previous week had already recorded around $1.28 billion, putting the combined two-week figure at $2.35 billion. Seven consecutive negative trading sessions accounted for roughly $1.91 billion of the retreat.

The daily pattern is revealing: withdrawals were not limited to one frightening session. Monday through Friday each ended in the red, with Wednesday and Thursday particularly heavy. NewsBTC covered the earlier five-day outflow streak, but the completed week's figures show that investors had not yet turned the tap back on.

BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust, IBIT, accounted for about $143.5 million of Friday's approximately $185.5 million in net withdrawals. Fidelity's FBTC made up roughly $41.9 million, while the other funds tracked reported no net flows for the session, according to the same dataset. It is tempting to read that as a judgement on either manager, but the more plausible interpretation is that investors use the largest and most liquid vehicles when adjusting exposure quickly.

The fact that a particular ETF experiences redemptions does not tell us whether shares were held by hedge funds, retail brokerage customers or other institutions. Nor does it reveal their reasons for selling. Portfolio rebalancing, risk limits and macro hedges can look identical in an aggregate daily flow table.

Bitcoin trades around the clock on spot exchanges and in derivatives markets. US-listed ETFs operate during market hours, and their creation-and-redemption processes connect the share market with underlying Bitcoin exposure. ETF data therefore offers a useful window, not a complete map, of demand. Large holders outside the products can still buy while funds lose money, and vice versa.

There is also a distinction between a withdrawal and a loss. If Bitcoin falls while ETF shares are held, the value of assets declines even without net redemptions. Conversely, a fund can experience inflows during a falling market. Keeping those measurements separate makes analysis much more useful than treating any red number as interchangeable.

The first signal to watch is whether the next US trading week brings even a modest return to positive daily flows. A second is the distribution across products: broad-based inflows would suggest more than one investor cohort is stepping back in. Finally, price stability without significant ETF buying would show whether the market has found demand elsewhere.

The broader institutional picture is not limited to daily flows. Changes affecting companies such as Strategy and Metaplanet underline how benchmark decisions and portfolio rules can influence crypto-linked exposure. For now, the sustained outflows are a warning about current appetite, not proof that the long-term ETF market has failed.

The price of XRP fell to $0.89 overnight on Nov. 15, and the cryptocurrency hit its lowest level in two years, according to TradingView. At the moment the price of XRP reached $0.89, Whale Alert flagged two transfers of 120 million XRP each, worth a combined $215.2 million. The transfers were made seven minutes apart, according to XRPSCAN and Bithomp data.

#5090. Anchorage Digital’s Stablecoins Can Now Settle Payments on Visa’s Network

Anchorage Digital’s Stablecoins Can Now Settle Payments on Visa’s Network

Anchorage Digital is extending its stablecoin reach into one of the world’s largest payment networks, teaming up with Visa to let select Anchorage-issued tokens settle transactions directly on VisaNet, starting with Western Union’s USDPT.

Under the arrangement announced Thursday, Visa and eligible companies can now use USDPT, a dollar-pegged stablecoin issued and custodied by Anchorage Digital Bank, to settle their obligations on the Visa network.

It’s the first Anchorage-issued token to gain that status, and the companies said the deal establishes a framework to add more of its stablecoins later.

The appeal, Anchorage argues, is pairing the speed of a stablecoin with the backing of a regulated bank. Anchorage operates what it bills as America’s first federally chartered crypto bank, overseen by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency.

“Speed alone won’t bring institutions onchain,” said Nathan McCauley, Anchorage’s co-founder and CEO, arguing that institutions want “a regulated institution behind the money,” now getting both a stablecoin’s speed and a federally regulated bank’s safeguards.

The move is the latest sign of Visa weaving stablecoins into its settlement plumbing.

The payments giant has built out a stablecoin settlement program spanning networks like Base, Polygon and others, launched a platform to help banks and fintech firms issue and move stablecoins, and has moved into onchain lending tied to its cards.

Dan Roesbery, a Visa vice president for crypto partnerships, framed the USDPT support as giving partners “another trusted, institution-grade option” for settling with Visa.

For Anchorage, the deal advances a broader ambition to become the settlement bank for stablecoins at institutional scale, not just issuing them but providing the custody and settlement rails underneath.

The bank already issues a roster of institution-grade stablecoins, including Tether’s U.S.-regulated USAT, Western Union’s USDPT, Ethena’s USDtb and others, each redeemable one-to-one for dollars. Its counterparty settlement network, Atlas, handles off-exchange settlement, collateral management and cross-border transfers.

Anchorage also recently positioned itself as the custody backbone of the U.S.-Mexico stablecoin corridor, custodying tokens on both sides of one of the world’s largest remittance routes. Backing a token on Visa’s network, which reaches merchants and banks worldwide, extends that institutional footprint further into mainstream payments.

The companies said support for additional Anchorage-issued stablecoins could follow the initial USDPT launch.

#5089. Bitcoin whales turn net long, retailers capitulate as BTC falls to $67K — Rebound coming?

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Bitcoin [BTC] closed in the red for the third consecutive day, with its price sliding to $67,000 on the charts. So far, the fall in prices has been driven by both whales and retail traders.

However, this pattern could be changing soon as Bitcoin’s sentiment starts to flip gradually. For instance, Hyperliquid whales turned back to the net long after two weeks of shorting BTC. This was the first selling period for them since March.

In fact, the daily mean of net long and net short grew from -1700 BTC on 8th November to around 900 BTC at press time. This seemed to imply that whales have been buying the dip below $70,000.

During the rally, which started in August, these whales went long. They subsequently sold the top. However, that does not guarantee that they will be right again.

On the other hand, retail traders have been showing signs of capitulation. In fact, BTC’s monthly change in Retail Investor Demand declined to around -10% after a sharp rise to over 17% as the price approached $80,000.

The same is the weakest reading since March. Back then too, Hyperliquid whales were net short on BTC.

This fall in participation by retailers, volumes below $10K, have been common during BTC’s correction.

When looking at historical patterns, it is clearly evident that when retailers capitulate, the prices tend to reverse. Thus, going against the crowd may help investors catch a move, either to the downside or the upside early enough.

Still, that does not mean that the contrarian signal always works. Even though it may be an ideal time to build positions.

Moreover, Bitcoin‘s Open Interest (OI) on Binance fell to $8.30 billion from $9.60 billion in November alone. This was its lowest level since 18th August, when BTC exploded past $65,000.

The slide below $68,000 triggered more long liquidations after those on the previous day. Over the past 24 hours, $1 billion were wiped out in crypto, with longs accounting for $863.3 million against $144.2 million in shorts.

This action forced leveraged traders out as supported by the sharp decline in OI. So, if BTC price stabilizes while OI stays at these levels, it would mean a rebound will be driven more by spot demand than leverage.

Therefore, whale positioning and retail capitulation could be a signal for a sustainable BTC recovery.

However, it needs to be backed by capital inflows from the market in the form of ETFs and spot buying, among others.
